## Which buildings are production lines

The real client sends `building.production.collect` only for buildings in `Global/EnumType.lua`'s `ProductLineBuilds`, plus the current season week card's farm building (1.0.364 Lua, `ProductLineManager:GetAllBuildIds`; static-analysis-only):

- **Core:** 10201000 Farmland, 10202000 Iron Mine, 10207000 Gold Mine, 10209000 Smelter, 10210000 Training Base, 10211000 Material Workshop, 10214000 Component Factory, 10221000 Oil Well, 10233000 Drone Parts Workshop, 10235000 Tactical Institute, and **10310000 Crystal Factory**, new in 1.0.364.
- **Season buildings in `ProductLineBuilds`:** 761000-765000, 771000-775000, 781000-785000 (Blessing Fountain), 801000-805000, and 822000-826000.
- **The current season week card's buildings**, from the `season_weekcard` table's `farm_building` and `farm_building_weekcard` columns. For Season 6, that's the four Spore Factory tiers (842000-845000) plus the Spore Factory week-card building (846000), which exists only if the card was bought.

Each season's set includes one week-card building: 764000, 775000, 785000, 805000, 826000, and 846000.

Crystal Factory (`LW_BUILD_CRYSTAL_STONE`) is the only `BuildingTypes` entry 1.0.364 added: 299 → 300, with nothing removed or renumbered. It belongs to the new Crystal system, and the client shows it only while `CrystalBuyDataManager:IsOpen` is true.

Six buildings that once looked like production lines aren't in either set: 10143000 Tactical Center, 10227000 Armament Institute (`LW_T11_Research`), and 10138000-10141000 Truck Station I-IV. Every collect attempt on them across 342 consecutive scheduled runs returned `errorCode=602026`, never `status=1` (confirmed live), and `goclient` no longer sends one.

The real client also never sends a collect for a building that isn't producing. `ProductLineManager:GetNextCollectTime` returns `-1` for a building with no `prodST` in its `building_new` entry, and when computed storage is 0 the client shows tip 602026 locally instead of sending anything. `goclient` mirrors the `prodST` rule.

Two details of the collect response, from the 1.0.364 Lua:

- The client treats a **missing or `-1`** `status` as failure and shows tip 602026. Every live success has carried `status=1`; what `status=0` means server-side is unknown.
- Locale `602026` reads "Production in progress. Please wait."

## Building and queue fields in `init`

Field meanings from the 1.0.364 Lua (`BuildingDate`, `QueueDataManager`, `Global/EnumType.lua`); static-analysis-only. Times are in ms.

**`building_new[]`**, one entry per building:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `uuid`, `bId`, `lv`, `pId` | Building instance, type id, level, and city tile |
| `sT` / `uT` | Upgrade start and end; `uT` is `0` when no upgrade is running |
| `state` | `0` normal, `1` upgrading, `2` folded, `3` paused, `5` crossing |
| `help` | Alliance help state: `0` none, `1` upgrade helped, `2` ruins helped, `3` both |
| `lCT` | Last collect, for the legacy collect buildings |
| `unaT` | Unavailable-from time |
| `pEndT` | Produce end, for the legacy collect buildings |
| `gValT` | Grow-value start, for the residential buildings that accrue items |
| `dStT` / `dEndT` | Repair start and end |
| `prodST` / `prodT` / `prodET` / `prodExtend` | Production line start, last tick, end (the cap), and stored amount |
| `prodStatus` | Production state; on camp buildings, the soldier level or equipment id being made |

**`queue_new[]`**, one entry per timed queue: `{uuid, qid, type, sT, uT, itemObj, funcUuid, para, para2, isHelped, lastHelpTime, helpNum}`. Builder queues add `{expireTime, unlock, gift, rentPrice, rentTime}`. `type` is a `NewQueueType` id, for example `3` hospital, `6` science, `117` rebirth hospital, and `120` T11 break; the full list is in the [Entity ID reference](/entity-id-reference).

A production line collects only when its stored amount is above 0. In the 1.0.364 Lua that's `prodExtend + num * floor((min(now, prodET) - prodT) / produce_time)`, with `produce_time` per building and level from the `building` table (milliseconds per tick). For example, the tick is 5 s for Farmland, Iron Mine, Gold Mine, Training Base, and the season farms, 60 s for the Oil Well, 1,800 s for the Smelter, Material Workshop, and Tactical Institute, 3 h for the Crystal Factory, and several hours for the Component Factory and Drone Parts Workshop, shrinking with level. Storage stops filling at `prodET` (static-analysis-only).

`collect_reward[]` lists pending world rewards with an expiry; its source ids are `CollectRewardType`, also in the [Entity ID reference](/entity-id-reference).

## Resource economy: two systems

**12 base resources** (`oil, metal, money, electricity, water, pvePoint, wood, people, dragonHonorScore, obsidian, flint, petroleum`) arrive embedded in most responses and standalone via `push.resource.info`. Separately, **"resource items"**, a keyed bag of stackable goods (soldiers-as-items, crafting materials), sync via `push.resource.item.update` / `user.get.all.resource.items`. There is no `get.storage.info` command; storage capacity is a client-computed sum over a stream of server-pushed effect deltas (`push.effect.change`), not a directly queryable value.

`docs/command-reference.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Command reference"
description: "How the client's dispatch commands (3,115 in the 1.0.364 Lua catalog, plus 54 C#-only and 133 chat-table wire names) break down by domain, direction, and transport channel, the conventions claim requests share, and where the full catalog lives."
---

Every command is dispatched off one flat string; there's no numeric opcode layer above SFS2X's own framing. In 1.0.364 the Lua catalog (`MsgDefines`) defines **3,115** commands, of which `MsgMap` gives a handler to 3,097; **54** more exist only in C#; and the chat subsystem's own table defines **133** wire names. The 1.0.351 figures were 3,065 / 3,047 for the Lua catalog and 131 for the chat table, 3,178 in all. This page summarizes how they're organized; the full row-level catalog is described below rather than reproduced as a giant static table.

## The 1.0.364 catalog at a glance

All counts are static-analysis-only, from a script that parsed every `Net/Msgs` `Message` class and every `SFSNetwork.SendMessage` call site:

| Direction | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Request | 2,243 | At least one Lua send site |
| Push | 731 | No send site and a `push.*` name, plus `init` |
| Never sent | 124 | No send site and not push-named: dead, or a server push with a request-style name |
| Request, indirect | 9 | Sent through a variable, for example `BatchDoServerMail(MsgDefines.X)` |
| Sent and push-named | 6 | Both |
| Request from C# | 2 | No Lua send site, but a C# message class |
| **Total** | **3,115** | 3,113 distinct wire names: two wire strings are defined under two keys each |

- **54 C#-only commands** never appear in `MsgDefines`, including the login plumbing (`login.ext`, `check.device.change`, `change.user.parseid`), the world-map viewport pulls, and the march and kick pushes. C# handles 71 wire names in all; for the 18 that are also in the Lua catalog, C# wins. See [Lua architecture](/lua-architecture#dispatch-order).
- **The chat table** has 133 wire names: 87 travel on the chat WebSocket, 45 on the game socket, and 1 has no handler. Five of them share a wire name with a `MsgDefines` command.
- About 23% of the Lua catalog (731 of 3,115) is server pushes.

## By functional domain

Two independent axes describe every command: which gameplay system it belongs to, and whether it's a client request or a server-initiated push (roughly a fifth of all commands are pushes, 22% in 1.0.351 by the `push.*` naming convention). The domain breakdown below was built against the 1.0.351 catalog and hasn't been redone for 1.0.364.

| Domain | Count | Priority | Covers |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Activity | 900 | **Deprioritize** | Time-limited live-ops: holiday events, gacha minigames, themed raids (~98 sub-features) |
| Season | 754 | **Deprioritize** | Recurring seasonal state-vs-state metagame: cross-server war, city occupation, alliance train |
| Alliance | 310 | **Core** | Guild membership, roles, world-map marks, mutual aid |
| Shop/Economy/IAP | 188 | **Core** | Real-money IAP, VIP subscriptions, trading center, storage shop |
| World Map | 166 | **Core** | Open world layer: marching, finding, radar, PVE encounters |
| City/Building | 110 | **Core** | Base building: construction queues, decoration, worker assignment |
| Military/Army | 87 | **Core** | Troop training, formations, hospital, research, equipment |
| Account/Login | 80 | **Core** | Session bootstrap, credentials, real-name auth, profile |
| Hero | 71 | **Core** | Hero leveling, star-up, gacha, fragment exchange |
| Task/Quest | 70 | **Core** | Chapter tasks, daily quests, hero dispatch/ghost recon missions |
| Government | 69 | **Core** | Server-wide political layer: king election, cabinet offices |
| PVP/Arena | 53 | **Core** | 1v1/3v3 asynchronous ladder + two rotating reskins |
| Chat | 31 | **Core** | World/alliance/rally channels, moderation, AI-chat feature |
| Mail | 27 | **Core** | Inbox: read/delete/claim, battle-report delivery |
| System | 26 | **Infra** | Maintenance notices, SDK plumbing |
| Admin/Debug | 7 | **Skip** | GM-only, debug-gated client-side |
| Misc | 108 | **Triage** | Leaderboards, player career/talent, photo album, titles |

These rows sum to 3,057, not the 3,047 mechanically-extracted main-table figure quoted above (and not the 3,178 grand total, which also includes the 131 chat-table commands this per-domain breakdown doesn't cover) -- a handful of commands land ambiguously between two domains and were counted in each, so this table is a categorization aid, not an exact partition.

## Changes in 1.0.364

An exact diff of the 1.0.351 catalog (`LWLF` 793, recovered from the CDN) against the 1.0.364 APK's (`LWLF` 825) gives:

- `MsgDefines` keys: 3,065 → 3,115. Handled commands (`MsgMap`): 3,047 → **3,097**.
- **50 added, 0 removed, 0 renamed** (same key, different wire string), and no handler moved.
- The live Android (826) and iOS (821) bundles match 1.0.364 at the catalog level.
- Every request schema `goclient` sends is unchanged. Some responses gained fields; for example, the `push.chat.get.system.mails` list push gained `delActivityIds`.

The chat table grew from 131 to 133 wire names but wasn't diffed entry by entry; the domain table above still describes 1.0.351. All of this is static-analysis-only.

| Module | Added | Commands |
|---|---:|---|
| CrystalBoss (new "Red Boss" activity) | 13 | `red.boss.get.march`, `red.boss.battle.report`, `get.red.boss.user.record`, `red.boss.get.achievement.info`, `red.boss.receive.achievement.reward`, `red.boss.get.progress`, `red.boss.claim.all {type}`, `red.boss.claim.daily.reward`, and 5 `push.red.boss.*` pushes |

| `Net.Msgs` root | 5 | `age.signal.record` (age-signal compliance), `exchange.goods.buy`, `world.alliance.expedition.info`, `world.give.up.alliance.building`, `push.bp.score.repair` |

Other 1.0.364 changes that touch protocol behavior: `ProductLineBuilds` gained the Crystal Factory (see [City & building](/city-building#which-buildings-are-production-lines)), `MailEnum` gained `CrystalBoss=58`, and the Lua `LoginErrorCode` table gained `55`-`58` (see [Identity, login & session](/auth#login-rejection-codes)).

A few commands the real client sends never appear in `MsgDefines`, because C# sends them directly: `change.user.parseid`, `check.device.change`, and `login.ext`. See [Identity, login & session](/auth#post-login-sequence). They're three of the 54 C#-only commands above.

## Claim requests

The 1.0.364 coverage pass catalogued **558 claim-like requests**, those whose names contain claim, collect, receive, reward, free, daily, sign, gift, or similar, each with its request params and the guard around its first send site; 55 carry a hand-traced eligibility rule. About 260 look like free claims; the rest are read-only fetches whose names merely contain "reward", spends, PvP actions, or purchases. Few are documented on these pages: of the 245 claim wires reachable from one partition of the UI, 231 appear nowhere in the docs. The conventions below are shared across them (static-analysis-only unless marked).

### Claim-all sentinels

Several claims take a sentinel instead of an id, to claim everything pending in one request:

| Request | Sentinel |
|---|---|
| `daily.quest.reward` | `stage: -1` claims every reached daily-activity chest; the response lists them in `stageArr` |
| `sign.receive.day.reward` | `day: 0` claims every claimable sign-in day |
| `activity.hero.score.reward` | `index: -1` claims every reached score chest |
| `new.arena.reward`, `gale.arena.reward` | `target: -1` claims every reached daily box |
| `season.tower.reward` | `stageId: -1` claims the group score rewards |
| `city.battle.activity.gain.task.reward` | `configId: -1` claims every task, `-2` every score goal |
| `city.competition.s0.gain.task.reward` | `cityLv: -1, configId: -1` claims the score tasks |
| `zone.mobilization.claim.challenge.reward` | `index: 0` claims every damage reward |
| `lw.receive.towerup.first.reward`, `lw.receive.dominator.up.first.reward` | `id: -1`, which the stage item sends; whether it claims every pending milestone is unverified |

### Other conventions

- **Claim state.** `TaskState` `1` (CanReceive) means claimable and `2` means claimed; other claim-state enums are in the [Entity ID reference](/entity-id-reference#wire-enum-values).
- **"Already claimed."** The generic error is `120289` (confirmed live for the VIP dailies, see [Live validation against production](/live-validation)).
- **Daily gates use the server day.** "Already claimed today" checks compare timestamps with the server day, which starts at 02:00 UTC live, see [Identity, login & session](/auth#server-day-and-daily-reset).
- **`activityId` types differ.** Almost every activity reward request takes `activityId` as an Int, but the generic activity detail read, `hero.event.info.get`, takes it as a UTF string.
- **The detail read sends the entry's `activityid`.** An `init` activity entry may carry an `activityid` besides its `id`, and the client sends that one (`ActivityInfoData.lua:126-128, 160-161`). The Alliance Duel is `{id: 55000, activityid: "70000"}`: asked for `"55000"`, the server answers a bare `{success=true}` (confirmed live). See [Alliance Duel](/alliance-duel#finding-todays-entry).
- **Free and paid variants can share a wire name.** A lottery with `useFree: 0` spends tickets or diamonds, `useGold`/`gold` flags spend diamonds, and `free.building.up.new` with `gold: 2` pays with diamonds.
- **Speed-ups.** `build.ccd.m.new`, `queue.ccd.m.new`, and `building.camp.accel` take either an item string (`itemIDs`, or `itemId` for the camp, as `"tmpl;n|tmpl;n"`) or a `useGold` amount. The UI's `isGold` flag never reaches the wire (`QueueCcdMNewMessage.lua:3-17`). `queue.ccd.m.new` with an empty `itemIDs` is the client's own diamond instant finish (`ArmyManager.lua:199-203`). The items-only `build.ccd.m.new` reply lists the items spent in `itemCostArr` and the diamond balance in `remainGold` (confirmed live), see [Alliance Duel](/alliance-duel#speed-ups).

### Reward payload

Claim responses carry a `reward` array plus, often, a sibling `resource` object (1.0.364 `RewardManager`; static-analysis-only):

```text
reward:   [ {type: Int, value: Int | Object, total?: Long}, ... ]
resource: {oil, metal, money, electricity, water, pvePoint, wood, people, dragonHonorScore, obsidian, flint, petroleum}
```

- `type` is a `RewardType` id; the full id-to-name table is in the [Entity ID reference](/entity-id-reference#resources-155).
- For plain resources and currencies (`OIL`, `METAL`, `FOOD`, `GOLD` for diamonds, stamina, and so on), `value` is the amount gained and `total` the new balance.
- For goods (type `7`), `value` is `{itemId, count, rewardAdd}`: `count` is the new owned count and `rewardAdd` the amount gained. Resource items (`27`) use `{id, num}`, heroes (`25`) `{heroId, rewardAdd, uuid}`, and soldiers (`23`) `{itemId, count}`.
- `resource` holds absolute balances, applied before the `reward` entries. Food is `money` on the wire.
- Some responses also carry a top-level `gold`, and a few counters arrive as their own top-level fields rather than as `reward` entries.

## Search the full catalog

Two row-level catalogs exist:

- **The 1.0.364 coverage catalog** (`commands.tsv`): all 3,115 `MsgDefines` commands, one row each, with the wire name, direction, runtime handler, request params with their SFS2X types (`name:Int`, nested arrays expanded, `[name:Type]` for conditional puts), the response fields the handler reads, the DataCenter managers it calls, the send-site count and first send sites, the C# handler where C# shadows Lua, duplicate-wire notes, and a relevance label. Companion indexes list every one of the 4,561 send sites with its enclosing function and nearest `if` guards (`command_send_sites.tsv`), the 558 claim-like requests (`claim_commands.tsv`), the 133-name chat table (`chat_commands.tsv`), and the 159 game systems (`systems.tsv`). These live with the coverage-analysis artifacts, outside this repo, and are regenerable with the method in [Findings & further work](/findings).
- **The 1.0.351 dossier catalog** (`cmd-data`), described below: 3,178 commands total, 3,047 from the main dispatch table (`Net.Msgs.*`, over the primary SFS socket) plus 131 from the dedicated chat subsystem's own table (`Chat.WebMessage.*` / `Chat.NetMessage.*`, split across the chat WebSocket and the primary socket, see the **WS** / **SFS** tags).

<Note>
The source dossier this page is derived from ships the full catalog as an interactive, client-side search tool (a search box filtering on key/wire-cmd/handler-class, plus a channel dropdown for **All channels** / **SFS socket** / **Chat WebSocket**, rendering up to the first 300 matches at a time). That live widget isn't reproduced here; hand-transcribing ~3,178 rows into a static Markdown table would be both unwieldy and error-prone. The underlying data is not lost, though: it's the same `cmd-data` JSON data island (one row per command, `[key, wire cmd, handler class, channel]`) backing the dossier's search tool, and it is regenerable directly from the client's own dispatch tables using the same mechanical extraction that produced it in the first place.
</Note>

Each row in the 1.0.351 `cmd-data` catalog carries four fields:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Key` | The internal message-class short name (for example `ShowStatusItem`, `TaskRewardGet`, `PushItemAdd`) |
| `Wire cmd` | The flat dot-separated string actually sent on the wire (for example `show.status.item`, `task.reward.get`, `push.item.add`) |
| `Handler class` | The fully-qualified decompiled handler/message class (for example `Net.Msgs.ShowStatusItemMessage`, `Net.Msgs.PushItemAddMessage`) |
| `Channel` | `SFS` (primary SFS2X socket) or `WS` (dedicated chat WebSocket) |

Commands whose `Key` is prefixed `Push` (wire cmd prefixed `push.*`) are server-initiated pushes rather than client requests; this is the 22% figure cited above.

The full 3,178-row dataset (extracted from `MsgDefines`/`MsgMap` for the main table, and the chat subsystem's parallel table for the 131 `Chat.WebMessage.*`/`Chat.NetMessage.*` entries) is available in the extracted reports produced alongside this dossier, and can be regenerated from the client using the extraction methodology described in [Extraction methodology](/methodology).

Field-level request/response schemas for the structurally central commands in each domain are documented in the gameplay-domain pages, not here; reading a command's own `OnCreate`/`HandleMessage` pair in the decompiled Lua is the authoritative source for anything not covered there. (See [City & building](/city-building), [Military, hero & battle](/military-battle), [Alliance, chat & mail](/alliance-chat-mail), [Shop, trading & real-money IAP](/shop-iap), and [World map](/world-map).)

`docs/data-tables.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Game data tables"
description: "The shape, container format, CDN path, split-table layout, and categorized index of the balance/config Lua data tables shipped alongside the client: 1,291 in 1.0.364."
---

1,291 balance/config tables in 1.0.364 (table version 39432, 1,049,915 rows), and 1,298 in the live set 39516. Each is a data-only Lua module compiled from what is clearly a spreadsheet pipeline: positional row arrays, a column-index descriptor, and a string-interning pool for repeated values. 1.0.351 shipped 1,279.

## Table shape

```lua
T.index = { id = {1,"number"}, cost_resource = {19,"string",true} }  -- field -> {col, type, isLinked?}
T.data  = { [10100000] = {10100000, "135104", ..., "30030;200|30031;200", ...} }
T.vExt  = { "1;30|14;30", ... }   -- interned strings, referenced by 1-based index when isLinked
T.link  = { [1]={9,512025}, [2]={512026,535161} }  -- split-table partition ranges, for the largest tables
```

Only 4 field types exist across the whole corpus: `string`, `number`, `array`, `table`. In 1.0.364 the column declarations break down as 8,641 `string`, 5,166 `number`, 587 `array`, and 78 `table`. Compound values are packed strings, almost universally `id;count` pairs joined by `|`. Very large tables (world monster spawns, army data) are physically split across sibling files, resolved via the `link` range table, see [Split tables](#split-tables) below.

## Container & versioning

A plain ZIP, one flat-namespace entry per table name, the odd `.data` extension is misleading; `unzip -l` works on it directly. The local version manifest is one line, `version,size,md5,crc32`, matching the filename `table_{version}_{md5}.data`. The 4th field is the archive's CRC32, not a timestamp: the 1.0.364 APK's `table/version` is `39432,19332173,<md5>,1911068049`, and both the MD5 and the CRC32 match the shipped archive. `ApplyUpdate` checks the size and CRC after patching (static-analysis-only). Table updates are tracked and patched (bsdiff) fully independently of the Lua bundle and asset bundles.

The 1.0.364 C# reads the current table version from the check-version `table_version` field (`version,size,md5[,crc][;patch chain]`). The server returns that field, and `locale`, only when the request carries `table_env=table_online`, which the real client always sends (confirmed live on 2026-10-05, see [Startup, version-check & hot-update](/bootstrap)). The 1.0.364 APK ships table version 39432 and locale 23557. On 2026-10-05 the server named table 39516 and locale 23570, the same numbers the iOS app's `resVersion` ended in on 2026-10-04: that tail is the device's local table and locale versions, see [resVersion](/bootstrap#resversion). Android and iOS got the identical `table_version` and `locale` (confirmed live).

The 1.0.364 coverage pass decompiled and loaded all 1,291 tables, read 26 of them row by row (building production, VIP, daily tasks, visitors, alliance gifts, subscriptions, dispatch, train, and DataConfig), and covered the rest from their schemas, sample rows, and reader modules. `season_weekcard`'s `farm_building` and `farm_building_weekcard` columns name each season week card's production buildings (see [City & building](/city-building#which-buildings-are-production-lines)).

### Table CDN

The table archive's CDN path has no app id and no platform segment, unlike the Lua bundle's (1.0.364 C# `TableFileUpdate`):

```text
https://lastwar-cdn.akamaized.net/hotupdate/table/table_{version}_{md5}.data
https://lastwar-cdn.akamaized.net/hotupdate/table/table_{new}_{old}.patch
```

- The full archive is a plain ZIP. HEAD requests on the APK's own archive returned 200 on all three CDN bases, with an ETag equal to its MD5, and the live 39516 archive downloaded as plain PKZip, not ChaCha-wrapped.
- A patch is a plain `BSDIFF40` file; the ChaCha `PURBDP` wrapping is optional. The client downloads one only when `client_config` switch 0 is on and its local version is in the `;old|size|crc` patch chain.
- The origin is the Aliyun OSS bucket `lastwar-client-us`; listing it returns AccessDenied.
- The live patch chain skips the APK build. On 2026-10-05 it listed 39500, 39487, 39323, 39277, 39273, 39267, 39250, 39228, 39191, and 39182, but not 39432, so a fresh 1.0.364 install downloads the full 19.5 MB archive instead of a patch.

### What changed in the live set (39432 to 39516)

The live 39516 archive was fetched on 2026-10-05 and diffed against the APK's 39432:

- **No schema change.** No table gained or lost a column.
- **8 tables added**, all pre-shipped A/B or "new" variants that no client Lua reads yet, for example `lw_world_monster_B`, `lw_hero_skill_B`, `lw_guide_flow_new`, and `detect_event_new`.
- **1 table removed**: `test_all_types`.
- **13 tables changed rows**: weekly server-group rotations (arena, zone war, champion duel, migration), event score thresholds in `activity`, two shop buy limits, and new goods, decorations, and stages.

Every table behind the production, VIP, daily-task, visitor, alliance-gift, subscription, dispatch, and idle-reward mechanics is byte-identical across the two versions.

## Split tables

10 tables are split, with 335 sub-tables between them: `exchange` (3), `lw_army` (12), `lw_monster` (31), `lw_monster_B` (31), `lw_monster_C` (27), `lw_monster_born` (73), `lw_monster_born_B` (73), `lw_monster_born_C` (51), `quest` (10), and `reward` (24). In 1.0.364 (static-analysis-only):

- The base table holds `index`, `vExt`, and `link`; its `data` is empty.
- Each `<base>_split<N>` holds `data` only, and its interned values index the base's `vExt`.
- To read a row, find the `link` range that contains the id, then open `<base>_split<index>`.

`LocalController` builds the sub-table name differently for names in its `OLD_STYLE` list: it asks for `<base><N>`, without `_split`. `reward` is in `OLD_STYLE`, but it ships as `reward_split1` to `reward_split24`, so the 34 `getLine`/`tryGetLine(TableName.RewardConfig, id)` call sites ask for a `reward<N>` entry that isn't in the archive. The only other source would be a `LuaDatatable` asset fallback, and the shipped `datatable` asset manifest holds only a placeholder, so as shipped those lookups return nil. The live 39516 set still ships `reward_split1..24`.

### A/B variant tables

`PlayerInfo:GetABTestTableName` picks a table variant from `init.user.monopoly_ab`, the server-pushed A/B slot (see [Findings & further work](/findings)). Value 18 selects the civilization-spark set (`building_B`, `lw_monster_B`, `lw_stage_feature_B`, `lw_guide_flow_B`, `monopoly_B`, and seven more `_B` tables), and value 1 selects `detect_level_B`. `building_B` has the same production numbers as `building`.

### Tables that aren't what their names say

- **`item` is the DataConfig table, not an item catalog**: 1,328 keys with columns `k1` to `k30`. The `init` push's `dataConfig` replaces it wholesale, so the shipped rows are only defaults.
- **267 non-split tables are shipped but never read by client code**, for example `daily_reward`, `lw_base_visitor_config`, `vip_privilege`, and `develop_simulation` (88,019 rows). They're server-side config that happens to ship with the client.
- `lw_monster_point` strings are GBK-encoded, not UTF-8.

## Categorized index (1.0.351, 1,279 tables)

This breakdown was built against the 1.0.351 archive and hasn't been redone for 1.0.364's 1,291 tables.

| Group | Count | Examples |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `lw_*`: core "live" gameplay tables | 601 | heroes, army, monsters, buildings, seasons (dominated by `lw_monster*` split-table fan-out, 304 files) |
| `activity_*`: live-ops events | 124 | boxopen, hunter, easter_egg, dig |
| `aps_*`: A/B variant family | 52 | factory, pve waves, heroes rank |
| `season*` (non-`lw_`) | 46 | landmine, pass, reward_group |
| `build*`/`city*`/`scene*` | 38 | building, city_car, construction_queue |
| `monster`/`pve`/`battle` related | 63 | boss_stage_reward, monster_refresh |
| shop/pay/gold related | 23 | goldbrick_and_price, import_vip_pay |
| alliance\* | 26 | alliance_resource, alliance_task |
| misc / long tail | 257 | daily_quest, government, chat_room, calendar, and a profanity-filter word list |

These rows sum to 1,230, not the full 1,279; they're the dominant categories, not an exhaustive partition. The remaining ~49 tables (hero/troop/army data, resource/economy, rank/leaderboard, guide/novice-flow, item/artifact, and a few UI/language tables) weren't individually bucketed.

`docs/entity-id-reference.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Entity ID reference"
description: "Numeric ID catalog for every building, monster, hero, troop line, resource, and item/equipment type the client can reference, extracted from Global_EnumType.lua and the table_decompiled data tables."
---

Every building, monster, troop, hero, resource, and equipment type the client can reference by numeric ID, extracted by a 6-agent parallel pass over `Global_EnumType.lua` (the master Lua enum repository, hundreds of small category tables) and the relevant `table_decompiled/*.lua` data tables, cross-referenced against the English locale strings for display names where a lookup path exists.

## By domain

| Domain | Entries | Primary source | Notable finding |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Building | 299 | `Global_EnumType.lua` `BuildingTypes` + `DragonBuildingTypes` (complete enums) | 5 sub-families: core city, legacy-named but still active (`FUN_BUILD`/`APS_BUILD` prefix, includes the main city-hall building `FUN_BUILD_MAIN` and farm/pasture/wormhole mechanics `APS_BUILD_*`), alliance territory, season-event, cross-server dragon |
| Monster | 170 | `LWWorldMonsterType` + `WorldMonsterSpecialType` enums, sampled from `lw_world_monster.lua` | Confirms world-map monsters are organized by resource-node type (`ResMetal`/`ResFood`/`ResGold`/...) with `Boss` as the single largest distinct-kind category |
| Resource | 155 | `Global_EnumType.lua` `ResourceType` + `RewardType` + 6 supporting mapping tables (complete) | `RewardType` is broader than currencies alone, includes `HOUSE`/`HOSPITAL`/`HERO`/`WORKER` as grantable "reward" categories |
| Item/Equip | 108 | `Global_EnumType.lua` item enums (complete) + equipment tier/slot catalog with real names | `item.lua` is NOT an item catalog (it's a generic config table), named equipment instead sourced from a tiered weapon/armor/core/radar catalog (M3→M6-A progression) |
| Hero | 66 | `table_decompiled/lw_hero.lua` filtered to `type=1` (real heroes) + category enums | 393 raw rows dedupe to ~43 real collectible heroes once PVP-dummy/skirmish-soldier/dominator stat-block rows are filtered out |
| Unit/Troop | 32 | `table_decompiled/lw_soldier.lua` + `soldier_eleven.lua` + category enums | Only 4 real troop "lines" exist, each a T1–T11 tier progression, no Infantry/Lancer/Marksman class split, unlike similar games |

<Info>
**Reading this table**: Not every domain's numbers work the same way. **Buildings**, **resources**, and most of **items/equipment** come straight from small, complete category enums, high confidence. **Monsters** mixes 2 complete category enums with a sample of the actual per-monster catalog (a 12,115-row per-level table deduped down to distinct kinds, not exhaustive by monster instance, but every distinct monster *kind* the sampling found is included). **Heroes** is a deduped, type-filtered view of a 393-row table that mixes real collectible heroes with reused stat-blocks for other game modes (PVP dummies, skirmish soldiers); only `type=1` (real heroes) plus category enums are included. **Units/Troops** is genuinely small: the player's own army has exactly 4 troop "lines" (each a T1–T11 tier progression), not a branching class system, see the table below for confirmation that Infantry/Lancer/Marksman-style class splits don't exist in this game's actual data.
</Info>

## Full entity catalog (830 entries)

The source dossier ships this catalog as an interactive, client-side search tool (a search box filtering on ID/name/category, plus a domain dropdown, rendering up to the first 300 matches at a time). That live widget isn't reproduced here. Instead, the full 830-row dataset, the same `ent-data` JSON data island backing the dossier's search tool, is broken out below as one Markdown table per domain, in full, since even the largest individual domain (Buildings, 299 rows) is far more readable as a static table than the combined set would be.

Each row carries four fields: **ID** (the numeric value used on the wire or in data tables), **Internal name** (the Lua enum member or internal string), **Display name** (the English locale string, where a lookup path exists, `-` where none was found), and **Category** (the specific enum table or data-table column the row traces back to).

Every question flagged during the client-building effort, and how it was resolved. Of the original 8 open items, a dedicated multi-agent research pass closed 6 outright, and live testing against production (see [Live validation against production](/live-validation)) closed the remaining 2. Two more items (enum numeric values, ShuMei/ACE enforcement) surfaced and were closed during that same live-testing pass, outside the original 8. The 1.0.364 analysis and live work in October 2026 then closed ten more questions and opened several new ones, and a full-coverage pass over the 1.0.364 APK corrected 21 claims across these docs (see the full coverage analysis below). This page tracks all of them, plus the narrow follow-on work that remains.

## Full coverage analysis (1.0.364)

In October 2026, eleven analysis agents went through the whole 1.0.364 APK with one rule: every unit gets accounted for. All of it is static analysis; a fact counts as live only where a line says so.

### Method

- **A ledger of units.** A script enumerated every unit of the APK into six ledgers: Lua modules, data tables, C# assemblies, Java packages, native libraries, and other files (resources, asset containers, manifests). That's **22,401 units**. Each agent claimed its units by group, and a checker verified that every unit was claimed. The final check reported `covered 22401/22401` with no problems. Its 11 "large group" flags are templated families (generated `Message` classes, Android resource directories, the `lw_monster` split tables), listed for review, not failures.
- **Four levels of coverage.** Every unit reached the first two:
  1. **Decompiled or parsed** into readable source or structured data: all 18,733 Lua modules (patched unluac), all 1,291 data tables (decompiled and executed into JSON), all 118 C# assemblies (ILSpy), the base APK's Java (jadx; one method body failed), and all 8,059 bundled UnityFS bundles. The native libraries were **not** decompiled: they got a symbol and string survey plus targeted arm64 disassemblies.
  2. **Mechanically indexed:** a script wrote a row for the unit into an index without anyone reading it, for example one row per command with its request params and SFS2X types, per C# type, per data table, and per bundle.
  3. **Summarized at group level** (`summarized`): the unit is covered by its group's write-up, which came from the index plus a read of the group's key files. That's 17,574 units, typically views, list cells, templated `Message` classes, vendor and platform libraries, resources, and art.
  4. **Read line by line** (`read`): 4,827 units, the logic layers: protocol, state managers, controllers, and bootstrap.

| Ledger | Units | Read | Summarized |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Lua modules | 18,733 | 4,493 | 14,240 |
| Other files | 1,813 | 241 | 1,572 |
| Data tables | 1,291 | 26 | 1,265 |
| Java packages | 407 | 45 | 362 |
| C# assemblies | 118 | 22 | 96 |
| Native libraries | 39 | 0 | 39 |
| **All** | **22,401** | **4,827** | **17,574** |

"Covered" doesn't mean "read". The main caveats: no native library was read, only surveyed; 3,022 of the 3,104 `Message` classes were parsed by script, and hand-checked samples matched on request params in 84 of 84 cases and on response fields in 77 of 84; and inside Assembly-CSharp, 130 types (about 11,500 lines) were read line by line while the other 3,539 were summarized from the type index and key methods. Anti-cheat and anti-fraud code (Tencent ACE, ShuMei, `psh`, the `init.add` challenge, `login.ext`, the probe template, and client-computed mini-game validation) was inventoried as a surface only, never analysed.

### Headline results

- **The command surface, fully indexed.** 3,115 `MsgDefines` commands, each with its request params and SFS2X types, the response fields its handler reads, and every one of its 4,561 send sites with the guards around them. 54 more commands exist only in C#, and the chat table adds 133 wire names. See [Command reference](/command-reference).
- **159 game systems mapped**, each with its managers, `init` fields, pushes, commands, timers, and resets.
- **21 corrections to these docs**, now applied. The largest:
  - The C# runtime is FM_Mono (Mono 6.13.0), not HybridCLR.
  - The world map does stream a viewport, through C#-owned block pulls, and season maps are 3000×3000.
  - `hotUpdateMsg` is `name,version,size,crc32`, and `resVersion`'s tail is local state.
  - The native chat transport behind `CalcChatSign` is unreachable, and the two `readygo.tech` cleartext endpoints are dead.
  - `free.building.upgrade.finish` and `queue.finish` are free collects, not paid instant finishes.
  - About 20 commands, not one, report client-computed battle results.
  - The alliance chat room id is deterministic, and `Scene/LWHummerScene` is the Armed Truck reward's own 3D scene.
  - The SFS2X library in use is SmartFox2X 1.7.8 plus the game's own `BaseUtils` transport; `Smartfox2xLw` is dead code.
- **New protocol facts**, added to the pages they belong on: the server-day boundary and reset events, the reward payload shape, error conventions, the XAssetPro container, the table CDN and split-table layout, the WebSocket preamble, the chat transport, the mini-game PvP transport, and the C#/Lua dispatch order.
- **A claim catalogue**: 558 claim-like requests, each with its parameters and the guard at its first send site, hand-traced for 55 of them. Most aren't in these docs; [Command reference](/command-reference) summarizes the conventions they share.
- **A never-automate inventory**: rewarded ads (the Android build ships no ad SDK at all), rating and survey rewards, account and role deletion, payments and diamond spends, irreversible moves, and client-reported results. Several share a wire name with a free claim and differ by one parameter, so they're catalogued to keep them out of automation by accident.
- **Two live checks.** Check-version returns `table_version` and `locale` only for `table_env=table_online`, and the live table set 39516 differs from the APK's 39432 in rows only, not in schema (both confirmed live on 2026-10-05).

The full row-level indexes (commands, claim commands, send sites, systems, tables, bundles, C# types) live with the analysis artifacts outside this repo and can be regenerated with the method above.

## Resolved in the 1.0.364 pass

- ~~**Does the shipped client send a `Handshake`?**~~: **Resolved** no. In 1.0.364, `NetConnection` handles only `a=1` (`Login`) and `a=29` (ping-pong) as system actions, and the connect path runs TCP connect, an `a=29` probe, then `Login` (static-analysis-only). The 2026-10-04 capture of the real iOS app shows no `a=0` on any socket. The server still answers a `Handshake` if one is sent. See [SFS2X wire protocol](/wire-protocol).
- ~~**Why an own-device `Login` gets `E005`**~~: **Resolved** the Android `Login` sent an empty `ta`. `goclient` filled `ta` only for iOS. C485 found from real Android captures that an Android `Login` with `{}` gets `E005` and one with the platform markers filled in doesn't ([discussion #22](https://github.com/ljagiello/lastwar-client/discussions/22)). On 2026-10-13 one build sent the 2026-10-04 own-device token twice, changing only `ta`: `{}` got `ec=28`, `ep=[E005]`, and the filled blob (`#os` = `Android`, `#bundle_id` = `com.fun.lastwar.gp`, `lw_platform` = `market_global`, plus the build and zone keys) logged in (confirmed live). The `deviceId` shape doesn't block it, and neither does device trust nine days after binding, since neither changed between the two runs. A guest `Login` is accepted with either `ta`. See [Identity, login & session](/auth#a-device-of-its-own).
- ~~**What `E005` means**~~: **Resolved** as far as the client goes. The 1.0.364 C# maps it to `ERROR_MAINTENANCE` and shows a maintenance dialog without touching credentials. Live, the server also returned it for a token presented under the wrong platform identity, so the label is the client's UI bucket, not the server's reason. See [Identity, login & session](/auth#login-rejection-codes).
- ~~**Tactical Center, Armament Institute, and Truck Station I-IV**~~: **Resolved** they aren't production lines. They returned `602026` on all 342 scheduled runs and never `status=1` (confirmed live), and none is in the 1.0.364 Lua's `ProductLineBuilds`. A `602026` response therefore doesn't confirm a command pairing. See [City & building](/city-building#which-buildings-are-production-lines).
- ~~**The `120471` per-donation cooldown**~~: **Resolved** it isn't a cooldown. The free donate path holds regenerating charges (`useNum` of `maxNum`, refilled every `refreshTimeBlock`), and `120471` means none is left (static-analysis-only). See [Alliance, chat & mail](/alliance-chat-mail).
- ~~**What the mail claim's `type` holds**~~: **Resolved** for the real client: an internal mail group id sent as a UtfString. `goclient` sends the raw mail type as an Int, and the server accepts it (confirmed live). Which value the server reads stays open. See [Alliance, chat & mail](/alliance-chat-mail).
- ~~**Where `resVersion`'s last two parts come from**~~: **Resolved** they're local state. The C# builds the tail from `CURRENT_TABLE_VERSION` and `LOCALE_VERSION`, the newest table and locale on the device, built-in or downloaded (static-analysis-only). Check-version does return `table_version` and `locale`, but only for `table_env=table_online`, which `goclient` doesn't send (confirmed live on 2026-10-05); that request returned 39516 and 23570, the iOS app's tail. See [Startup, version-check & hot-update](/bootstrap#resversion).
- ~~**What the forward header's id means**~~: **Resolved** statically: it's the zone number, `ParseSid("APS783") = 783` in `BaseUtils`, which matches the `0x030F` in the 2026-10-04 capture. A second capture on another zone would confirm it live.
- ~~**Which id the Alliance Duel detail read takes**~~: **Resolved** the `init` entry's `activityid`, not its `id`. The duel's entry is `{id: 55000, activityid: "70000"}`, and `ActivityInfoData` lets `activityid` override `id` (static-analysis-only). Asked for `"55000"`, the server answers a bare `{success=true}`; asked for `"70000"`, it returns the full `eventList` (both confirmed live on 2026-10-06). The live entries carry their day window as `st`/`et`. See [Alliance Duel](/alliance-duel).
- ~~**Whether an items-only speed-up touches diamonds**~~: **Resolved** for `build.ccd.m.new`. With only `itemIDs`, the reply's `remainGold` equaled the starting balance and `itemCostArr` listed every item spent (confirmed live on 2026-10-06). `queue.ccd.m.new` and `building.camp.accel` haven't been sent live yet. See [Live validation against production](/live-validation#alliance-duel-and-duel-spend-commands).
- ~~**Whether `at.time` is an issue time or an expiry**~~: **Resolved** an issue time. A GSL `opt=login` response on 2026-10-04 carried `at.time` and `rt.time` equal to the moment of issue, in unix seconds (confirmed live), consistent with the 1.0.364 client's 30-day refresh rule. Whether the server also expires tokens on its own, and so what caused the 2026-10-02 rotation, stays open. See [Live validation against production](/live-validation).

## Open questions

These came out of the 1.0.364 static analysis and the October 2026 live work. Static analysis can't settle any of them; each needs a live observation.

- **Minimal `ta` content.** Reconnect works with `ta`'s device sub-fields blank (confirmed live), and an Android `Login` into an established account needs it filled (confirmed live, see the resolved `E005` item above). Which keys the server reads hasn't been isolated: the A/B tests compared `{}` with the whole blob, and the platform markers (`#os`, `#bundle_id`, `lw_platform`) are only the likely ones.
- **`dataConfigMd5` persistence.** The real client sends a server-issued value; in the 2026-10-04 capture it equaled `init.add.a` from the same session. Comparing `init.add.a` across two captures of the same app build would show whether the client persists it or the server echoes back whatever arrives. This is an integrity surface, so the question is about understanding the protocol, not about sending the value.
- **Does `opt=refresh` rotate `rt`?** The real client stores whatever non-empty `rt` arrives. If a refresh rotates `rt`, a token pair shared between the real app and a Go client keeps working only for whichever side refreshes first. On 2026-10-13, eight days after issue, three refreshes of the own device's pair each returned the current `at` with its original `at.time` and no `rt` (confirmed live). What a refresh returns once `at` is 30 days old is still open. See [Identity, login & session](/auth#refreshing-the-access-token).
- **Can two devices hold working sessions for one account?** This decides whether a Go client with its own device identity could keep its own tokens alongside the real app's. The 1.0.364 role-switch flow (email verification, `loginKey`, GSL `opt=login`) is how a device gets its own pair. GSL issued one to a newly bound Go-generated device on 2026-10-04, and that device's `Login` was accepted on 2026-10-13 (both confirmed live). The same night a second Go device was bound and logged in, and the first device's config still logged in afterwards, so their tokens coexist (confirmed live). Each `Login` takes the role's one live connection. Whether the real app's token stays valid alongside them is still open.
- **Which command collects the Tactical Chip Factory?** The 1.0.364 Lua reads both ways: `BuildBubbleManager` sends `building.camp.collect {uuid}` for chip buildings, and the factory's own UI sends `chip.collect {}`. One read of the factory's `building_new` entry in a captured `init`, then one capture of the real collect tap, would settle it. See [City & building](/city-building).
- **Does the live `init` carry `real_timezone_offset`?** The C# applies it only when present, and the Lua falls back to UTC without it, which would move its day boundary from 02:00 to 00:00 UTC while `tomorrow` stays at 02:00. The 2026-10-04 capture shows the key in the `Login` response; listing the top-level keys of a captured `init` would settle it. See [Identity, login & session](/auth#server-day-and-daily-reset).
- **Does the server check `platform` on `opt=refresh`?** The real iOS client sends `platform=iOS`; `goclient` always sends `Android`. A refresh token is scarce, so this hasn't been tested.
- **`status=0` from `building.production.collect`.** The Lua treats only a missing or `-1` status as failure; every live success has carried `status=1`.
- **When does each Alliance Duel action book its points?** Radar tasks book at the claim (confirmed live, 2026-10-07): each `receive.detect.event.reward` was followed by `push.act.score.obtain` with `addScore`, and `detect.event.help.end` produced none. Still open for UR secret tasks, power gains, and troop training: start, finish, or claim. `goclient` now logs every `push.act.score.obtain` with the request sent before it, which answers this per action from ordinary runs. See [Alliance Duel](/alliance-duel#the-score-push).
- **Are unclaimed duel chests mailed at the day's end?** A mail template for it exists in the locale; no live observation yet.
- **Is an empty or over-count `itemIDs` charged in diamonds?** An empty `itemIDs` on `queue.ccd.m.new` is the client's own diamond instant finish (`ArmyManager.lua:199-203`). What the server does with more items than are owned is unknown. `goclient` never sends either, so this stays a static reading.

## Resolved by live testing

See [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for full methodology.

- ~~**Does a finished radar task survive its `endTime`?**~~: **Resolved** yes (confirmed live, 2026-10-06). Nine tasks finished but left unclaimed were still listed by `get.detect.info` in state `1`, 46 minutes after their `endTime`. The unclaimed rescue task among them was kept too. Only unstarted tasks expire.
- ~~**Enum numeric values** (`BuildingTypes`, ...)~~: **Resolved** the authoritative `BuildingTypes` table lives in `Global_EnumType.lua`, giving every building's internal codename and numeric ID directly. See the [Game entity ID reference](/entity-id-reference) for the full extraction across buildings/monsters/units/heroes/resources/items.
- ~~**Whether the server enforces ShuMei/ACE anti-cheat data on login**~~: **Resolved** no ShuMei-specific block exists, as far as live testing shows. Reconnecting to an account with real history first looked ShuMei-gated, but that block turned out to be a token-identity mismatch (see the reconnect bullet below). On 2026-10-04 a captured iOS session reconnected into the established account with `shumeiBoxId` sent empty (confirmed live), and new-guest-account creation never needed it. Full test matrix in [Live validation against production](/live-validation).
- ~~**The missing post-login `init` push**~~: **Resolved** none of the three previously-identified leads were the cause. The real bug: `packet.go`'s `ReadPacket` already correctly detected the server's Zstandard-compressed packets (header bits `0x20` compressed + `0x10` useLZ4-repurposed-as-Zstd) but decompression itself was never implemented, it just returned an error, which every read loop indistinguishably treated as "connection closed." Fixed by adding a real Zstd decoder (`github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd`, a shared lazily-initialized `zstd.Decoder`) in that same branch. The post-login init push turned out to be ~313KB of Zstd-compressed `SFSObject` data on the wire; decoding it surfaced two further binary-codec bugs in `sfsobject.go`: `LONG_ARRAY`/`FLOAT_ARRAY`/`DOUBLE_ARRAY`/`BOOL_ARRAY`/`SHORT_ARRAY` (tags 9, 11, 13, 14, 15) were simply unimplemented, and `BYTE_ARRAY` (tag 10) was decoded with the wrong length-prefix width (i16 instead of the real i32), silently corrupting decode of any packet containing one, see the corrected wire-format table in [SFS2X wire protocol](/wire-protocol). Once both were fixed, the init push arrived cleanly on the very first attempt: no reconnect loop, no extended timeout needed, and the active-pull `login.init` fallback never had to fire. Of the two mechanisms built earlier to chase this symptom, only the three-attempt reconnect-on-timeout loop was unnecessary and has been removed (max login attempts back to 1); the halfway active-pull `login.init` send inside `waitForInitPush` was kept in place, unconditionally, as a real, still-exercised fallback for a genuinely silent server, not reverted, see [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for the full mechanism split.
- ~~**The established-account reconnect block**~~: **Resolved** not anti-fraud, not device fingerprinting, not session locking. Captured live traffic from the real iOS/Mac-Catalyst app (`/Applications/Last War.app`) via `tcpdump` against the same account, decoded the Login packet field by field (the SFS2X game socket is plain TCP, no TLS), and confirmed by a byte-for-byte raw replay that the same access token works cleanly across repeated connections, it is not single-use, and there is no rate-limit or already-connected mechanism. The actual gate: a token is bound to the exact `packageName`/`platform`/`appVersion`/`versionCode` identity it was issued under, and `goclient` hardcoded an Android identity unconditionally even when replaying an iOS-issued token. Fixed in `identity.go` (`BuildLoginParams` gained an `IOSMode` switch covering `packageName`, `packageSign`, confirmed still `SHA1(packageName)` on iOS too, `platform`, `pf`, `appVersion`, `versionCode`, the iOS-only `idfa`/`idfv`/`phone_native_screen` fields, removal of Android-only fields, and, at the time, populating `ta` with real captured content instead of an empty placeholder), plus `crossserver.go` and new `-cs-ios`/`-cs-at` flags in `main.go`. A real reconnect through the Go client's own from-scratch SFS2X implementation then succeeded cleanly: Login OK, followed immediately by a correctly Zstd-decoded init push showing the account's 162 real buildings. Caveat: the exact minimal required content of `ta` wasn't isolated, only that the full real captured blob worked, at the time of that capture. A later security fix replaced `ta`'s `LwDeviceID`/`LwShumeiID`/`LwAirKey` sub-fields with empty-string placeholders (they were leaking the same live device secrets in cleartext inside an opaque JSON string); reconnect is now **re-confirmed working with those placeholders** against the shipped code, an unattended cron running this client reconnected and collected real resources over multiple days (August 2026), re-verified after a live zone-server migration, so the server does not require `ta`'s real device sub-fields. What's left is even narrower: the *minimal* required `ta` content still isn't isolated (a different token needs its own fresh `ta` regardless, since session-specific fields live inside it), and a fully from-scratch login without a captured token hasn't been tried, see [Live validation against production](/live-validation).

## Resolved by a dedicated research pass

Full findings, with file:line citations into the client source, follow below.

- ~~**March "recall home" encoding**~~: **Resolved** not a coordinate sentinel, it's the literal enum constant `MarchTargetType.BACK_HOME = 3` (`Global_EnumType.lua:3945`), sent in the ordinary `target` field of `world.march.change` (the same command used to redirect a march anywhere), with `path` set back to the player's home-city tile. Full call chain traced from the UI button through to the wire request.
- ~~**`WorldPointInfo.proto`'s actual transport**~~: **Resolved** the "no confirmed call site" framing was outdated: `world.get.new` and `world.get.block`'s response field `points` (an array of raw byte blobs) is decoded via `WorldPointInfo.Parser.ParseFrom` in `WorldPointManager.ParseWorldGetBlock`, feeding the ~30 concrete point-type classes that render the world map. A second, nested call site decodes march destination points the same way.
- ~~**Four unrecoverable proto schemas**~~: **Resolved** all four (`ScoreProgressInfo`, `WorldCityRankMail`, `LwScoutReport`, `ShieldInfo`) were fully recoverable, and not where prior analysis stopped looking, see the callout below.
- ~~**`libxlua.so`'s `CalcChatSign`/AES/MD5 helpers**~~: **Resolved** the "no call site" claim was a tooling false-negative (this environment's `grep` is `ugrep`, which silently skips binary files without `-a`). The real call site was already sitting in report 06 (`ChatNetManager:InitWebSocketInst`, an alternate native-transport branch). That branch turned out to be unreachable in 1.0.364: only the armeabi-v7a `libxlua` registers `rg_websocket`, arm64's `luaopen_native` doesn't, and `LuaEntry:__InitCModule()`, the only code that would expose the native socket, is never called, so chat always uses the C# `ChatService` (static-analysis-only). The formula finding stands. Direct ARM64 disassembly of the native function (it ships unstripped, with symbols) confirms it's exactly `MD5(MD5(appId+uid) + timestamp)`, plain, unkeyed, textbook MD5, byte-identical to the already-known C# formula. Proprietary-crypto risk downgraded from "unknown" to confirmed **none**.
- ~~**`PlayerInfo:GetABTestTableName`**~~: **Resolved** not a hash or local computation, it's a single server-pushed integer, `monopoly_ab`, delivered in the post-login `Init` payload's `user` object. Each value (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 16, 18 in this build) is a reserved slot for one named A/B test; the function's `Is<TestName>B()` checks compare against it directly. A reimplementation cannot derive this offline, it must be read from a real login response.
- ~~**Season vs. Activity domain boundary**~~: **Resolved** (accuracy-measured, not just re-asserted): a genuine random sample of 100 commands (50 Season, 50 Activity) checked against actual handler code came back **97% label-defensible**. The 3 confirmed misclassifications aren't random noise, they're all cases where a single feature's sibling commands got torn across both domains because the classifier operates per-command/per-folder rather than per-`DataCenter`-manager (e.g. the Desert Storm fishing minigame's 8 commands split ~50/50 because one cmd string happened to contain `"fish.pond"`, a substring the classifier's ordered rule list catches before the generic `"season"` fallback).

<Check>
  **Bonus finding: 18 proto schemas recovered, not just 4.** The "unrecoverable" verdict on the four proto schemas stopped at "not in the Lua bundle" without checking two other places they actually live. Three of the four (`ScoreProgressInfo`, `ShieldInfo`, `LwScoutReport`) turned out to have full `Google.Protobuf`-generated C# classes in `Assembly-CSharp.decompiled.cs`, each embedding its complete compiled `FileDescriptorProto` as a base64 blob. All four, `WorldCityRankMail` included, which has zero C# presence at all, are also physically shipped as Unity `TextAsset`s inside a custom-packed AssetBundle blob (`assets/AssetBundles/BundleFragment0.bytes`, 525MB, indexed by a name→offset table also in the APK). Locating and extracting that bundle's `gameres_main_dir_proto` entry recovered **all 18** `.proto.bytes` files the client ships (not just the 4 originally sought) as serialized `FileDescriptorSet` binaries, decoded to human-readable `.proto` text and cross-validated field-for-field against the independently-recovered C# descriptors. Both the raw binaries and decoded schemas are saved at `extracted/recovered_protos/*.proto` / `*.decoded.txt`.
</Check>

`docs/gate-server-crypto.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Gate-server RSA+AES handshake"
description: "How the GSL (Gate Server List) HTTP exchange's hybrid RSA+AES-ECB envelope encryption works, and how to reproduce it in Go."
---

The "GSL" (Gate Server List) HTTP exchange is wrapped in a hybrid RSA+AES scheme. It looks like textbook envelope encryption at a glance, but the AES mode is ECB, not CBC, which turns out to make the whole thing simpler to reproduce, not harder.

<Warning>
  **Correction made during analysis.** The C# source sets `Mode = (CipherMode)2`. It's tempting to assume that's CBC, it's not. `System.Security.Cryptography.CipherMode`'s real ordinals are `CBC=1, ECB=2, OFB=3, CFB=4, CTS=5`. **`(CipherMode)2` is ECB.** This was confirmed both by reading the enum and behaviorally: encrypting the same plaintext twice with the same key produces byte-identical ciphertext (the ECB signature), and decryption succeeds regardless of which unrelated cipher instance performs it, impossible under CBC. There is no IV because ECB has none to give.
</Warning>

## Sequence

1. Client generates a random 20-character salt (from an 84-char alphabet, non-cryptographic `System.Random`, the exact PRNG doesn't matter to the server, only the resulting bytes do).
2. Salt is **RSA-PKCS1v1.5-encrypted** against the server's public key (delivered fresh every check-version response as base64 DER, no PEM armor) → base64 → URL-safe → this is the `uuid` POST field.
3. The AES key is derived as `ASCII(lowercase_hex(MD5(salt)))`, 32 ASCII bytes, **not** the raw 16-byte MD5 digest.
4. The request body (form-encoded device/session fields) is **AES-256-ECB-PKCS7** encrypted with that key → base64 → URL-safe → the `data` POST field. (Effective key size is 256 bits despite the source visually setting `KeySize = 128`, .NET's `Key` setter silently overrides it based on the 32-byte key length actually assigned.)
5. Response: if the top-level JSON has a non-empty `bin` field, decrypt it the same way (same salt-derived key) and re-parse as the same response shape.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| RSA padding | PKCS#1 v1.5 (OAEP explicitly disabled) |
| RSA key source | `resMsg` field, base64 DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`, delivered per-session |
| AES algorithm | AES-256 (RijndaelManaged, effective 256-bit key) |
| AES mode / padding | **ECB** / PKCS7, not CBC |
| AES key derivation | `ASCII(hex(MD5(salt)))`, 32 ASCII bytes used directly as the key |
| AES IV | None: ECB has no IV concept |
| Encoding | base64 → URL-safe (`+`→`-`, `/`→`_`, strip `=`) |

## Request fields

The plaintext form body that step 4 encrypts joins its fields with `&`, without URL-encoding. In 1.0.364 (static-analysis-only), the UnityWebRequest path sends:

```text
uuid=<deviceId>, airKey, loginFlag=1, country=<fromCountry>, is3D=1, lang, simOp,
platform, newServer=1, isSimulator, zone=<cached zone>, gameuid=<gameUid>,
openCountry=<storefront>, [opt, loginKey | rt]
```

This inner `uuid` is the device id, not the outer `uuid` POST field that carries the RSA-encrypted salt. The BestHTTP path sends the same fields with `newServer` after `gameuid`, and `goclient` matches the BestHTTP order. `platform` is `"Android"` on Android and `"iOS"` on iOS; `goclient` always sends `"Android"` and an empty `zone`. How the client picks `opt`, and what the response's `code` field means, are on [Identity, login & session](/auth#token-lifecycle).

The crypto itself is unchanged in 1.0.364: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, a 20-character salt, and AES-256-ECB keyed by `hex(MD5(salt))`, with URL-safe base64.

## Go implementation

```go
// 1. Parse resMsg as a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo directly, no PEM step needed in Go
pub, _ := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(derBytes)
rsaPub := pub.(*rsa.PublicKey)

// 2. Random 20-char salt, any charset/CSPRNG is fine
salt := randString(20)

// 3. uuid field
ct, _ := rsa.EncryptPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, rsaPub, []byte(salt))
uuid := urlSafeB64NoPad(ct)

// 4. AES key
sum := md5.Sum([]byte(salt))
key := []byte(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]))   // 32 ASCII bytes, NOT the raw digest

// 5. data field, AES-256-ECB-PKCS7 (Go's stdlib has no ECB mode;
//    loop block.Encrypt() once per 16 bytes, ECB has no chaining)
data := urlSafeB64NoPad(aesECBEncryptPKCS7(formBody, key))

// POST {gate}/gameservice/getserverlist.php  body: uuid=...&data=...
// response.bin, if present: aesECBDecryptPKCS7(urlSafeB64Decode(bin), key)
```

<Note>
  **Same AES-ECB scheme, reused elsewhere.** The identical `AESDecrypt` function is reused, with a hardcoded key, to decrypt a server-pushed Lua snippet (`init.add.data`) that's fed directly to an `eval`-equivalent (`GameEntry.Lua.Env.DoString`); the result goes back to the server in `login.ext` (see [Identity, login & session](/auth#post-login-sequence)). That snippet is an integrity challenge, so this project documents it as a protocol fact only and leaves the key out. Elsewhere the same client also uses a properly-chained AES-CBC-with-explicit-IV helper for a Zendesk webchat URL, so the ECB choice for GSL is a deliberate (if weak) design decision for that one path, not a general "forgot the IV" bug.
</Note>

```

`docs/go-client-roadmap.mdx`:

```mdx
---
title: "Go client implementation roadmap"
description: "The recommended build order for a from-scratch Go client, plus a step-by-step guide to building, configuring, and actually running the researcher's own Go implementation."
---

Everything documented elsewhere in this dossier translated into a build order. Bootstrap first, core loop second, everything else is additive.

## Phase 1: Bootstrap (nothing else works without this)

1. `GET getlsu3dversion.php`, extract `resMsg` (RSA pubkey) and the answering host. An `updateType` of `2` means the server no longer accepts the build you claim ([Startup, version-check & hot-update](/bootstrap)).
2. Implement the GSL RSA-PKCS1v15 + AES-256-ECB-PKCS7 envelope ([Gate-server RSA+AES handshake](/gate-server-crypto)), Go has no stdlib ECB mode, write the trivial 16-byte-block loop.
3. `POST getserverlist.php`, check `code` (`0` is success), parse `serverList[]`, pick the entry matching the last-logged server (else the first), and persist `at`/`at.time`/`rt`/`rt.time`. The [token lifecycle](/auth#token-lifecycle) covers how the real client picks `opt` and refreshes.
4. Open a plain TCP socket to the zone's gateway. `serverList[].ip` is a `|`-delimited list; the real client races every entry and keeps the first to answer its ping ([SFS2X wire protocol](/wire-protocol#gateway-race-and-the-pre-login-probe)). Implement the packet envelope, the length-derived XOR "encryption," zlib compression, and the `SFSObject` codec ([SFS2X wire protocol](/wire-protocol)).
5. Send SFS `Login` with the ~50-field parameter object ([Identity, login & session](/auth)), including the `SecurityCode`/`OneCode`/`CoreV` MD5 constructions.
6. Wait for the bare `init` push; live, it arrives on its own, with no `init.before` or `init.after`. Capture `chatToken` if chat is needed later.
7. Start a 4-second `PingPongRequest` heartbeat.

[Live validation against production](/live-validation) has a side-by-side table of what the real client does on the wire and which of `goclient`'s simplifications the server accepts.

## Phase 2: Core loop

Build the command dispatch table directly from the extracted `cmd-data` catalog (see [Command reference](/command-reference) for the row schema and how to regenerate it, don't hand-transcribe the ~3,178 rows by hand). Implement, in order: **City/Building** → **Military/Army** (the base-building + troop loop) → **World Map** (needed for march/PVE) → **Alliance + Chat + Mail** (high command-count payoff) → **Hero** → **Shop/Economy**.

## Phase 3: Defer

Season (754 cmds) and Activity (900 cmds) are recurring/time-limited live-ops content, 54% of the entire protocol surface by command count, and it churns every patch. Implement only if a specific feature is explicitly wanted; treating either as a monolith is not advisable given how fragmented each sub-feature's schema is.

## Crypto primitives checklist

| Primitive | Go path |
|---|---|
| RSA PKCS1v15 encrypt | `crypto/rsa.EncryptPKCS1v15`, drop-in |
| AES-256-ECB-PKCS7 | `crypto/aes` + hand-rolled block loop (stdlib omits ECB deliberately) |
| MD5-hex-as-key | `hex.EncodeToString(md5.Sum(...))`, exact match |
| URL-safe base64, no padding | `base64.URLEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding)` |
| ChaCha8 (patch obfuscation) | hand-rolled, `x/crypto/chacha20` is hardcoded to 20 rounds |
| zlib inflate/deflate | `compress/zlib`, stdlib |
| Zstandard (battle reports, LZ4-flagged packets) | `github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd` |
| bsdiff/bspatch (table/asset patches) | `github.com/gabstv/go-bsdiff` or similar |

---

## Running the Go client

The roadmap above was actually built, the repository root is a from-scratch Go reimplementation of this protocol, live-tested against production (see [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for the full writeup of what's confirmed against live production servers). It's **fully working and live-confirmed** for GSL crypto, SFS2X packet framing (including Zstandard decompression), the SFSObject codec, brand-new-guest-account login, email-verification account binding, resource collection across 14 confirmed building types (Farmland, Iron Mine, Gold Mine, Smelter, Material Workshop, Training Base, Oil Well, Drone Parts Workshop, Component Factory, Tactical Institute, and the four Season 6 Spore Factory tiers; the 1.0.364 Crystal Factory and the Season 6 week-card building are wired in but unconfirmed, see the building-type table), and a growing set of account-level automations, none of which are building-`uuid`-scoped: the "Armed Truck"/"Overlord" idle rewards (`lw.pve.idle.reward`), greeting city visitors (`visitor.operate`), bulk-helping alliance members (`al.help.all`), claiming all alliance gifts (`alliance.reward.allreceive`), claiming all mail (`chat.get.system.mails` + `mail.reward.batch`), donating to the alliance's currently-recommended tech (`science.data.refresh` + `al.science.donate`), and both once-a-day VIP claims (`vip.add.login.score`, `vip.get.every.day.reward`), see [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for the full writeup of each. Reconnecting into an *established* real account's live game state was proven working end-to-end when first captured; that capture used the `ta` analytics blob's real device/anti-fraud sub-fields, which a later security fix replaced with empty-string placeholders, and reconnect is now **re-confirmed still working with those placeholders** (an unattended cron reconnected and collected real resources over multiple days, August 2026). What remains open is the *minimal* required `ta` content and a fully from-scratch login without a captured token; see [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for the current state.

<Note>
  **Not yet general-purpose.** The reconnect path needs a session config: one captured from a real client login, or, since 2026-10-13, one `-own-device-session` writes for a device of its own (see below). A from-scratch login using `-cs-ios`-equivalent identity from the very first GSL call hasn't been tried yet. An own-device config refreshes its access token on its own (see [Refreshing the access token](/auth#refreshing-the-access-token)), but a captured config has no refresh token, so when the server invalidates its access token (`ec=28`, `ep=[E011]`, as on 2026-08-16 and 2026-10-02), the fix is a fresh capture, see [Recovering from a rotated token](/capturing-and-decoding-traffic#recovering-from-a-rotated-token).
</Note>

This section walks through going from a clean checkout to a working `-collect` run.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Build">
    ```bash
    go build -o lastwar-client ./cmd/lastwar-client
    go test ./...
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Set up a session config (recommended)">
    Reconnecting into an established account needs several values that can only come from a real client's own login (device ID, access token, ...). The ShuMei fingerprint is optional: a captured session reconnects with `shumeiBoxId` empty (confirmed live, 2026-10-04) — see [ShuMei device fingerprint](/shumei). Rather than typing them on the command line every time, put them in a JSON file:

    ```bash
    cp config.example.json ~/.lastwar_goclient_session.json
    chmod 600 ~/.lastwar_goclient_session.json
    # then edit it with your own real values
    ```

    `~/.lastwar_goclient_session.json` is auto-loaded on every run if present, no flag needed. To use a different file, pass `-config /path/to/file.json`. Individual `-cs-*` flags still override whatever the config file says, for one-off tests.

    ```json
    {
      "zone": "your-real-zone-e.g.-APS1234",
      "gameUid": "your-real-composite-gameUid",
      "deviceId": "your-real-device-id_n3d",
      "shumeiBoxId": "your-real-shumei-fingerprint-token",
      "accessToken": "your-real-access-token-from-a-captured-login",
      "iosMode": true,
      "appVersion": "1.0.344",
      "versionCode": "786"
    }
    ```

    **Where these values come from:** capture a real login (e.g. `tcpdump` while the real app logs in, since the SFS2X game socket is plain TCP with no TLS) and let `pcap -session-out` write this file from the captured `Login`, see [Recovering from a rotated token](/capturing-and-decoding-traffic#recovering-from-a-rotated-token). [Capturing and decoding traffic](/capturing-and-decoding-traffic) also covers the manual pipeline. The game server's `ip` (a `|`-delimited list of the zone's gateways, tried in order) and `port` are optional: without them, `goclient` looks the role's server up with GSL `getserverlist`, and it looks again if a saved address stops answering, see [Looking up the game server](/auth#looking-up-the-game-server). The access token is not single-use, but it *is* bound to the platform identity (`iosMode`) and the build (`appVersion`/`versionCode`, optional, defaulting to built-in values) it was issued under, and it will eventually need refreshing from a fresh capture.

    <Warning>
      This file contains live credentials for a real account, keep it out of version control. It's already outside the repo, in your home directory, and `chmod 600`'d above; don't move it into this repo or commit it anywhere.
    </Warning>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Run a collection pass">
    ```bash
    # One-time setup above, then everything below just works with no flags.

    # Collect resources from all confirmed buildings, the Armed Truck/Overlord idle rewards, greet visitors,
    # help alliance members, claim all mail and alliance gifts, donate to the recommended alliance tech,
    # and claim both daily VIP bonuses:
    ./lastwar-client -collect

    # Just list buildings without collecting:
    ./lastwar-client -list-buildings
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Other ways to run it

```bash
# Optional features: list them (name, on/off, default, duel policy), then run one once.
# Turn one on for -collect with the session config's "features" map.
./lastwar-client -list-features
./lastwar-client -run daily-quests

# A feature held for the Alliance Duel is refused on a day whose duel entry doesn't list its
# score types; -run-anyway runs it regardless (see Alliance Duel):
./lastwar-client -run radar-claims -run-anyway

# Stay connected and issue ad-hoc test commands without re-authenticating:
mkfifo /tmp/lw_cmd_pipe
./lastwar-client -interactive /tmp/lw_cmd_pipe &
echo 'building.production.collect {"uuid":123}' > /tmp/lw_cmd_pipe

# Override specific config fields for a one-off test (e.g. a different captured token):
./lastwar-client -collect -cs-at <a-different-access-token>

# Brand-new guest account instead (always works, no email or config needed):
./lastwar-client -list-buildings -no-config

# Bind a guest session to a real account via email verification (only needed once,
# to obtain a fresh config -- see the dossier for turning that into a session config):
mkfifo /tmp/lw_code_pipe
./lastwar-client -email you@example.com -code-pipe /tmp/lw_code_pipe &
echo 123456 > /tmp/lw_code_pipe
```

Device identity also persists across runs in `~/.lastwar_goclient_*` (deviceId, username, gameUid, loginKey) independent of the session config, so repeated guest/email-flow runs present a consistent device to the server. Delete those files to start fully fresh. Set `LASTWAR_STATE_DIR` to keep them in another directory instead, so several device identities can coexist on one machine.

```bash
# A device of its own, set up in one run: bind it by email verification (-server <number> picks another role),
# trade its loginKey for its own token pair (GSL opt=login), and write a session config:
mkfifo /tmp/lw_code_pipe
LASTWAR_STATE_DIR=~/.lastwar_own_device ./lastwar-client -email you@example.com \
  -code-pipe /tmp/lw_code_pipe -own-device-session ~/own_device_session.json &
echo 123456 > /tmp/lw_code_pipe
```

Since 2026-10-13 a `Login` with the resulting config works, and it refreshes its own tokens. Run it like any session config, `LASTWAR_STATE_DIR=~/.lastwar_own_device ./lastwar-client -config ~/own_device_session.json`. Whether the own device's session leaves the real app's tokens valid is still open, see [Identity, login & session](/auth#setting-up-a-device-of-its-own-in-one-run).

Last War is a Unity game with almost none of its logic compiled into the app you download. Three independent, independently-updatable layers sit on top of a thin native core, and only the crypto and wire protocol are what a Go client needs to reimplement.

## Client architecture

The client is built on Unity, but the game's C# isn't IL2CPP-compiled at all. `libil2cpp.so` is FunPlus's **FM_Mono** bridge: it exports the il2cpp ABI and runs the managed code on upstream Mono 6.13.0. Instead of compiled game code:

- **Gameplay logic and UI**, city building, army/hero systems, world map, alliance, chat, mail, shop, and nearly every network command (3,115 in the Lua catalog), is written in **Lua** (18,733 compiled modules in 1.0.364, hot-updated as one bundle).
- **Engine glue and platform integration**, the network stack, the crypto, asset/resource management, the world-map viewport protocol, and third-party SDK wiring, lives in **hot-updatable C#**: 118 XOR'd `.mdl` assemblies that FM_Mono loads at startup. The `dllres` hot-update manifest lists replacements for 117 of them (`mscorlib` has no entry), and `noUpdateAssemblies.json` pins `SmartFox2X` to the APK copy, so the SFS2X data-model library changes only with an app release, unless a hot update replaces the pin list itself (static-analysis-only).
- **The static core**, `libil2cpp.so` (the FM_Mono bridge), the Mono runtime, the Unity engine, and the native xLua library, is what's actually fixed at app-store-release granularity. It contains no game logic at all (see [Native binaries & security](/native-binaries)).

Two transports carry traffic to FunPlus's servers:

- **HTTP(S)** for bootstrap, version check, hot-update manifests, and gate-server discovery (the "GSL" flow), wrapped in a custom RSA+AES hybrid scheme.
- **A raw TCP socket** speaking a hand-rolled reimplementation of [SmartFoxServer 2X](https://www.smartfoxserver.com/)'s binary `SFSObject` protocol, carrying every gameplay command as a string `cmd` (e.g. `"mail.read"`) plus a typed key/value payload.

### What a Go client actually needs

Only two of these three layers matter for protocol compatibility: the **crypto** ([Gate-server crypto](/gate-server-crypto)) and the **wire format** ([SFS2X wire protocol](/wire-protocol), [Command reference](/command-reference)). The Lua/C# split is a client-implementation detail, a Go client talks TCP and HTTP directly and never touches Lua. The [native-binary survey](/native-binaries) exists to answer one practical question: does anything below the protocol layer (anti-cheat, device attestation, signing) block a clean-room client?

<Check>
  **Short answer**: no, for creating and driving new guest accounts, and for binding a guest session to a real account via email verification, both confirmed live, end to end, repeatedly. Reconnecting into an *already-established* account's live game state is confirmed live too, including against the shipped code after a security fix swapped part of the `ta` blob for placeholders (an unattended cron reconnected and collected real resources over multiple days, August 2026). It's just not yet fully general-purpose: it still needs a captured access token and server address, see [Native binaries & security](/native-binaries) and [Live validation against production](/live-validation) for the full scope and current state.
</Check>

```

Everything documented elsewhere in this dossier up to this point was static analysis of a client the researcher owns, accurate, but unverified against a real server. This section documents what happened when the roadmap in [Go client implementation roadmap](/go-client-roadmap) was actually built (source at the repository root, a from-scratch Go reimplementation) and driven against the real production servers for a real account. It corrects a few static-analysis guesses, confirms most of them exactly, and documents one open problem static analysis alone could never have found.

## What's proven end-to-end

| Flow | Result |
