`internal/shumei/shumei.go`:

```go
// Package shumei reimplements the ShuMei (数美) device-fingerprinting
// registration flow the SDK performs against /deviceprofile/v4, enough to
// obtain a real `shumeiBoxId` for the Login request — instead of relying on
// the empty placeholder the game server also accepts.
//
// The Login's `shumeiBoxId` is what the SDK's getDeviceId() returns: `"B"` +
// the server-assigned `smid` (88 chars) once one exists, or a `"D"`-prefixed
// local fallback before that. It is never needed for the client to work: an
// empty `shumeiBoxId` is a first-class, accepted path (confirmed live).
//
// Reconstruction sources (all byte-exact where noted):
//
//   - the Obfuscator-LLVM-hardened `libsmsdk.so` (string decryption via
//     emulation of the 22 `.datadiv_decode*` init functions);
//   - `com.ishumei.smantifraud.SmAntiFraud` / `l11l11lI1lll` / `l111l1111lI1l`
//     / `l1l11I1l` / `l11l111llI1l` / `l11l11l1l1Il` / `l1l1l111Il`
//     decompiled from classes6.dex;
//   - `com.sdkmanager.SmSdkManager` (the game's own SDK wiring).
//
// The flow, end to end:
//
//  1. SmSdkManager configures the SDK: organization "9dNCYkjHeFMYZMOjxgX8",
//     appId "default", an X.509 certificate as the public key, area
//     AREA_FJNY, and it overrides the SDK's region-pinned fengkongcloud.com
//     hosts with a proxy at shumei-api.lastwargame.com:19091.
//
//  2. The SDK collects device data (the SubCollector/AbsDetector chain plus
//     the native `w1`), then protects it with a hybrid scheme: a 16-char
//     random nonce `r` whose MD5 (lowercase hex) is the AES-256 key, the
//     device-data JSON raw-deflated and AES-256-CBC encrypted under that key
//     (IV "0102030405060708"), and `r` itself RSA-OAEP(SHA-256)-wrapped with
//     the embedded certificate as `ep`.
//
//  3. The profile JSON is POSTed to /deviceprofile/v4 as
//     Content-Type: application/octet-stream. The body is
//     {organization, os, appId, encode:2, compress:3, data, tn, ep}.
//
//  4. The reply is {"code":<int>,"detail":{"deviceId":...},
//     "requestId":"..."}. code 1100 success, 1902 the server's generic
//     "can't use this" reply (any body it can't decode), 1903 hard error.
//
// Status (live-tested 2026-10-11): the full device-data fingerprint below,
// protected with the hybrid scheme, returns code 1100 and a real smid. The
// server validates the protection: an empty or minimal `data`/`tn`/`ep`
// returns 1902. The device-data template is a spoofed Android device profile
// (the client runs on a desktop, not a phone), so the smid it mints is for a
// device that does not exist — see the note in BoxID.
package shumei

import (
	"bytes"
	"compress/flate"
	"crypto/aes"
	"crypto/cipher"
	"crypto/md5"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Organization and AppID are the values the shipped game (Last War)
// configures the SDK with in SmSdkManager.callCreate(). They are
// app-specific identifiers, not SDK secrets.
const (
	Organization = "9dNCYkjHeFMYZMOjxgX8"
	AppID        = "default"
)

// OSName is the device-profile's `os` field (l11l11lI1lll.l111l1111l1Il). The
// SDK version "3.14.3" (l11l11lI1lll.l111l11111I1l) is not a deviceprofile
// field: it is the cloudconf request's `sdkver`, and here only the `a7` slot
// inside the protected device data (with "build1" in `a136`).
const OSName = "android"

// Region the game selects (AREA_FJNY) and the numeric area code the SDK
// derives from it (l11l11lI1lll.l1111l111111Il: "bj"->"001", "xjp"->"010",
// "fjny"->"011"). The game overrides the region-pinned host with a proxy, so
// the area code matters only as documentation of the intended datasite.
const (
	RegionName = "fjny"
	RegionCode = "011"
)

// DefaultDeviceProfileURL is the game's ShuMei device-profile endpoint
// (SmSdkManager.setUrl). The SDK's own built-in hosts are region-pinned on
// fengkongcloud.com and listed below for the record; Last War bypasses them
// entirely with this proxy. setUsingHttps(true) is the scheme.
const DefaultDeviceProfileURL = "https://shumei-api.lastwargame.com:19091/deviceprofile/v4"

// The SDK's built-in region hosts (l11l11lI1lll.java). AREA_XJP ->
// fp-sa-it(.fengkongcloud.com) / api-fp-retry-sa; AREA_FJNY -> fp-na-it-acc /
// api-fp-retry-na; default (bj) -> fp-it / api-fp-retry-bj, each paired with
// an api-fp-retry-* retry host. The game sets its own URL above, so these are
// documentation of the SDK's datasites, not something this client connects to.
const (
	SDKHostBJ   = "fp-it.fengkongcloud.com"
	SDKHostXJP  = "fp-sa-it.fengkongcloud.com"
	SDKHostFJNY = "fp-na-it-acc.fengkongcloud.com"
)

// Response codes from l1l11I1l.java: 1100 is success, 1902 asks the client to
// retry later, 1903 is a hard error. The smid lives under the reply's
// "detail" (l1l11I1l.l11l1111I11l) object as "deviceId" (l11l111llI1l.java).
const (
	CodeSuccess = 1100
	CodeRetry   = 1902
	CodeError   = 1903
)

// EncodeShape/CompressShape are the numeric values the native `w1` writes into
// the profile's `encode`/`compress` fields (see the FUN_00180d30(2.0, ...) and
// FUN_00180d30(3.0, ...) calls in the decompiled libsmsdk.so): "base64" and
// "deflate" in the SDK's protection pipeline.
const (
	EncodeShape   = 2
	CompressShape = 3
)

// ishumeiSPKIBase64 is the 2048-bit RSA SubjectPublicKeyInfo extracted from
// the embedded X.509 certificate (CN=e.ishumei.com, OU=SM, C=CN) the game
// passes to SmOption.setPublicKey. The SDK parses the certificate via
// CertificateFactory("X.509").generateCertificate(...).getPublicKey() and
// encrypts the payload with this key's public half.
const ishumeiSPKIBase64 = "MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAgtU+mYnt48Oq2QKKOKER" +
	"lBycUvFTynQvzoOrv172NxDsqco+IdfgFOB+WGrOQ3RRRdB/j8v+zS/9NZt4qJag" +
	"zxZytjb7OhcJ0vJAJLgPF4YcziZJHLSegBm36D7iCjUORsafVo2zDRU5bHTrMdLR" +
	"JN2dtGOOt9b23ClOmw1cIHUGY/uO/3WX0uIUNvvnIqGum2+ePzcEs6cILeCQZDJk" +
	"dNlPKUMxV1k/x+LGqy8H7tcjWgEW5gtCBD+qx0OxRZzzaakxdzVBjNDMWwPDUt0Q" +
	"Pm0QNeaspTibBDic9wAhJx6PPToq3YrkKBpPlQHtwpdyrJatfo/PoRd53lCVNC6Z" +
	"bwIDAQAB"

// MaxResponseSize bounds the device-profile HTTP response, mirroring
// gsl.MaxGSLResponseSize's rationale (a tiny JSON never needs more).
const MaxResponseSize = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB

// Client is the minimal client interface; *http.Client satisfies it. Keeping
// it as an interface lets tests inject a fake transport the same way the
// gsl/auth packages do.
type Client interface {
	Do(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error)
}

// DeviceProfile is the JSON body POSTed to /deviceprofile/v4. Field names are
// byte-exact from the native `w1` (FUN_0010f8d0 and the FUN_0010c160 it calls,
// in the decompiled libsmsdk.so):
// organization, os, appId, encode (2), compress (3), data, tn, ep. The first
// request carries no `retry` field (only the background resend adds it).
type DeviceProfile struct {
	Organization string `json:"organization"`
	OS           string `json:"os"`
	AppID        string `json:"appId"`
	Encode       int    `json:"encode"`   // 2 = base64
	Compress     int    `json:"compress"` // 3 = deflate
	Data         string `json:"data"`     // AES-256-CBC(raw-deflate(aNN-json))
	TN           string `json:"tn"`       // RSA-OAEP(cert, "0"), ignored by the server
	EP           string `json:"ep"`       // RSA-OAEP(cert, r), the AES key source
}

// ProfileResponse mirrors the device-profile reply: {code, detail{...},
// requestId}. `detail.deviceId` is the ShuMei device fingerprint (smid).
type ProfileResponse struct {
	Code   int `json:"code"`
	Detail struct {
		DeviceID    string `json:"deviceId"`
		OldDeviceID string `json:"oldDeviceId"`
		SID         string `json:"sid"`
		C           int    `json:"c"`
		T           int    `json:"t"`
	} `json:"detail"`
	RequestID string `json:"requestId"`
}

// ErrUnassigned is returned when the server replies without a deviceId (e.g.
// code 1902, its generic "can't use this body" response).
var ErrUnassigned = errors.New("shumei: device-profile reply carried no deviceId")

func publicKey() (*rsa.PublicKey, error) {
	der, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(ishumeiSPKIBase64)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("shumei: decode embedded public key: %w", err)
	}
	pub, err := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(der)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("shumei: parse embedded public key: %w", err)
	}
	rsaPub, ok := pub.(*rsa.PublicKey)
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("shumei: embedded key is not RSA (got %T)", pub)
	}
	return rsaPub, nil
}

// randomNonce returns a 16-char random alphanumeric string, the `r` the native
// `w1` generates per request.
func randomNonce() (string, error) {
	const alnum = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
	b := make([]byte, 16)
	for i := range b {
		n, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, big.NewInt(int64(len(alnum))))
		if err != nil {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: random nonce: %w", err)
		}
		b[i] = alnum[n.Int64()]
	}
	return string(b), nil
}

// aesKeyFromNonce derives the AES-256 key from `r`: MD5(r) as lowercase hex
// ASCII (32 bytes). This is the native `w1` scheme (FUN_0010c160).
func aesKeyFromNonce(r string) []byte {
	sum := md5.Sum([]byte(r))
	return []byte(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]))
}

// pkcs7Pad pads data to a multiple of blockSize using PKCS#7 (identical to the
// Java AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding the SDK uses).
func pkcs7Pad(data []byte, blockSize int) []byte {
	padding := blockSize - len(data)%blockSize
	return append(data, bytes.Repeat([]byte{byte(padding)}, padding)...)
}

// protect reproduces the native `w1` protection pipeline for the device-data
// JSON: raw deflate -> AES-256-CBC (key = MD5(r), IV "0102030405060708") ->
// base64, plus RSA-OAEP(SHA-256) of `r` (as `ep`) and of "0" (as `tn`).
func protect(pub *rsa.PublicKey, innerJSON string) (data, ep, tn string, err error) {
	r, err := randomNonce()
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", "", err
	}
	key := aesKeyFromNonce(r)

	// raw deflate (RFC 1951, no zlib header) — matches the SDK's deflate stage.
	var compressed bytes.Buffer
	zw, err := flate.NewWriter(&compressed, flate.DefaultCompression)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: deflate: %w", err)
	}
	if _, err := zw.Write([]byte(innerJSON)); err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: deflate write: %w", err)
	}
	if err := zw.Close(); err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: deflate close: %w", err)
	}

	// AES-256-CBC with the fixed IV "0102030405060708".
	block, err := aes.NewCipher(key)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: aes: %w", err)
	}
	iv := []byte("0102030405060708")
	padded := pkcs7Pad(compressed.Bytes(), block.BlockSize())
	ct := make([]byte, len(padded))
	cipher.NewCBCEncrypter(block, iv).CryptBlocks(ct, padded)
	data = base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(ct)

	// RSA-OAEP(SHA-256, MGF1=SHA-256, empty label) of `r` and of "0".
	epBytes, err := rsa.EncryptOAEP(sha256.New(), rand.Reader, pub, []byte(r), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: rsa-oaep ep: %w", err)
	}
	tnBytes, err := rsa.EncryptOAEP(sha256.New(), rand.Reader, pub, []byte("0"), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: rsa-oaep tn: %w", err)
	}
	return data, base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(epBytes), base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(tnBytes), nil
}

// Device holds the fingerprint values that change during a device's life: the
// clocks the SDK samples on every collection, the Wi-Fi details it reads when
// the app may see them, and the values one install keeps. BoxID fills each
// zero clock, Wi-Fi IP and collection time with the host's real value or a
// random one. It never makes up install values: the caller passes them.
type Device struct {
	// Now is the collection time, a9 (System.currentTimeMillis()). Zero means
	// the current time.
	Now time.Time

	// BootTime is when the device booted, a40 (the SDK's median of 11
	// currentTimeMillis()-elapsedRealtime() samples). a171 (elapsedRealtime())
	// and a170 (uptimeMillis()) count from it. Zero means Now minus the host's
	// uptime.
	BootTime time.Time

	// WiFi adds the connected network's details. Nil is what a real Last War
	// install sends: the SDK reads them only when the app holds
	// ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (l1l11l1Illl), Last War doesn't request it, so a19,
	// a30 and a31 come back empty and the serializer leaves them out.
	WiFi *WiFi

	// Install is what this install keeps between registrations. It must be
	// filled (NewInstall or Install.Fill): BoxID refuses one with values unset
	// rather than invent a phone the caller never sees, so the install sent is
	// always the one the caller keeps.
	Install Install

	// CollectTime is how long the SDK took to collect the device data, a133
	// (the milliseconds from the start of l111l1111llIl's collection to the
	// end). Zero means a random time from 150 to 600 ms.
	CollectTime time.Duration
}

// WiFi is the connected network, as Android's WifiInfo reports it to an app
// holding the location permission.
type WiFi struct {
	SSID  string // a30, unquoted: getSSID() adds the quotes
	BSSID string // a19, the access point's MAC
	IP    string // a31, the device's IPv4 on that network; "" means the host's LAN address
}

// withHostDefaults fills d's zero clocks and Wi-Fi IP with the host's real
// values and a zero CollectTime with a random one. It leaves Install as given.
func (d Device) withHostDefaults() Device {
	if d.Now.IsZero() {
		d.Now = time.Now()
	}
	if d.BootTime.IsZero() {
		d.BootTime = d.Now.Add(-hostUptime())
	}
	if d.WiFi != nil && d.WiFi.IP == "" {
		w := *d.WiFi
		w.IP = hostIP()
		d.WiFi = &w
	}
	if d.CollectTime == 0 {
		d.CollectTime = randDuration(150*time.Millisecond, 600*time.Millisecond).Truncate(time.Millisecond)
	}
	return d
}

// sdkStartLead is how long before collecting the device data the app started
// the SDK (SmAntiFraud.create), whose clock a80 records.
const sdkStartLead = time.Second

// deviceData builds the device-data JSON that protect encrypts: innerTemplate
// plus deviceID and d's clock, Wi-Fi and install values. It serializes the way
// the SDK's reflection serializer (l1l1l11Ill) does: compact, and without
// top-level entries that are empty strings, lists or maps. d must already
// carry its host defaults.
func deviceData(deviceID string, d Device) (string, error) {
	if d.BootTime.After(d.Now) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: boot time %s is after the collection time %s",
			d.BootTime.Format(time.RFC3339), d.Now.Format(time.RFC3339))
	}
	in := d.Install
	if in.AndroidID == "" || in.MediaDrmID == "" || in.PUUID == "" || in.FirstInstallTime.IsZero() || in.LastUpdateTime.IsZero() {
		return "", errors.New("shumei: install values are unset (Install.Fill sets them)")
	}
	if err := in.Validate(); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: install: %w", err)
	}
	if _, ok := in.For(deviceID); !ok {
		return "", errors.New("shumei: the install belongs to a different deviceId")
	}
	dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(innerTemplate))
	dec.UseNumber()
	var m map[string]any
	if err := dec.Decode(&m); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: parse device-data template: %w", err)
	}

	m["a2"], m["a97"] = deviceID, deviceID
	now, boot := d.Now.UnixMilli(), d.BootTime.UnixMilli()
	m["a9"] = now
	m["a40"] = boot
	m["a171"] = now - boot
	// uptimeMillis() leaves out deep sleep. The host's sleep time isn't
	// measured, so this equals elapsedRealtime().
	m["a170"] = now - boot
	start := d.Now.Add(-sdkStartLead).UnixMilli()
	m["a80"] = fmt.Sprintf("%d-%s", start, javaRandomDigits(start, 5))
	m["a133"] = d.CollectTime.Milliseconds()

	m["a24"] = in.AndroidID
	m["a84"] = in.MediaDrmID
	m["a163"] = in.PUUID
	m["a125"] = map[string]any{"fit": in.FirstInstallTime.UnixMilli(), "lut": in.LastUpdateTime.UnixMilli()}
	m["a126"] = in.BoxID
	var saved int64
	if !in.BoxIDSavedAt.IsZero() {
		saved = in.BoxIDSavedAt.UnixMilli()
	}
	m["a167"], m["a168"] = saved, saved

	if w := d.WiFi; w != nil {
		m["a19"] = w.BSSID
		if w.SSID != "" {
			m["a30"] = `"` + w.SSID + `"`
		}
		m["a31"] = w.IP
	}

	for k, v := range m {
		if isEmpty(v) {
			delete(m, k)
		}
	}
	var b bytes.Buffer
	enc := json.NewEncoder(&b)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	if err := enc.Encode(m); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: marshal device data: %w", err)
	}
	return strings.TrimSuffix(b.String(), "\n"), nil
}

// isEmpty reports whether the SDK's serializer would skip v: null, an empty
// string, an empty collection or an empty map (l1l1l11Ill.l111l11111lIl).
func isEmpty(v any) bool {
	switch v := v.(type) {
	case nil:
		return true
	case string:
		return v == ""
	case []any:
		return len(v) == 0
	case map[string]any:
		return len(v) == 0
	}
	return false
}

// javaRandomDigits returns n digits drawn with java.util.Random(seed).nextInt(10).
// a80 is the SDK start time in milliseconds, "-", then five such digits seeded
// with that same time (l11l11Il11l).
func javaRandomDigits(seed int64, n int) string {
	const multiplier, mask = 0x5DEECE66D, 1<<48 - 1
	s := (uint64(seed) ^ multiplier) & mask
	digits := make([]byte, n)
	for i := range digits {
		for {
			s = (s*multiplier + 0xB) & mask
			bits := int32(s >> 17) // next(31)
			v := bits % 10
			// nextInt(bound)'s rejection test, relying on int32 overflow as Java does.
			if bits-v+9 >= 0 {
				digits[i] = byte('0' + v)
				break
			}
		}
	}
	return string(digits)
}

// BoxID registers a device with the ShuMei backend and returns its assigned
// device fingerprint, already prefixed with `"B"` to match the Login request's
// `shumeiBoxId` field. deviceID should match the request's own deviceId so the
// server can bind the fingerprint to the same device identity. dev carries
// the install values, which must be filled (see Device.Install), and the clock
// and Wi-Fi fields; zero clocks and no Wi-Fi report the host's clocks and no
// Wi-Fi, like a real Last War install.
//
// Note on scope: the device-data fingerprint this mints is a spoofed Android
// profile for a device that does not exist. The game server does not require a
// real shumeiBoxId (an empty one is accepted), so this is an optional
// best-effort path, not a hard gate.
func BoxID(client Client, deviceID string, dev Device) (string, error) {
	pub, err := publicKey()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return boxID(client, pub, deviceID, dev.withHostDefaults())
}

// boxID is BoxID with the RSA key as a parameter, the same way protect takes
// it, so a test can use its own key pair and decrypt the POSTed body. dev must
// already carry its host defaults.
func boxID(client Client, pub *rsa.PublicKey, deviceID string, dev Device) (string, error) {
	inner, err := deviceData(deviceID, dev)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	data, ep, tn, err := protect(pub, inner)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	profile := DeviceProfile{
		Organization: Organization,
		OS:           OSName,
		AppID:        AppID,
		Encode:       EncodeShape,
		Compress:     CompressShape,
		Data:         data,
		TN:           tn,
		EP:           ep,
	}
	body, err := json.Marshal(profile)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: marshal profile: %w", err)
	}

	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, DefaultDeviceProfileURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: build request: %w", err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
	req.Header.Set("Connection", "Close")

	resp, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: post device profile: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()

	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, MaxResponseSize))
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: read response: %w", err)
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: unexpected status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, truncate(raw))
	}

	var pr ProfileResponse
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &pr); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("shumei: parse response: %w", err)
	}
	if pr.Detail.DeviceID == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w (code=%d)", ErrUnassigned, pr.Code)
	}
	return "B" + pr.Detail.DeviceID, nil
}

func truncate(b []byte) string {
	if len(b) > 256 {
		return string(b[:256]) + "..."
	}
	return string(b)
}
```

```go
import (

// fakeTransport returns a canned device-profile response, recording the
// request body so the test can assert on the exact wire shape.
type fakeTransport struct {
	body    []byte
	content string
	status  int
}

func (f *fakeTransport) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	f.body, _ = io.ReadAll(req.Body)
	f.content = req.Header.Get("Content-Type")
	return &http.Response{
		StatusCode: f.status,
		Body:       io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader([]byte(`{"code":1100,"detail":{"deviceId":"smid-test-0123456789","sid":"s-1","c":1,"t":1700000000},"requestId":"r-1"}`))),
		Header:     http.Header{},
	}, nil
}

// TestBoxID drives boxID with a test-generated key pair, so besides the wire
// shape it can decrypt the POSTed body and check each protected field holds
// what the server expects: ep wraps r, tn wraps "0", and data is the device
// data for this deviceID.
func TestBoxID(t *testing.T) {
	priv, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rsa.GenerateKey = %v", err)
	}
	ft := &fakeTransport{status: http.StatusOK}
	client := &http.Client{Transport: ft}

	const deviceID = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_n3d"
	dev := testDevice()
	got, err := boxID(client, &priv.PublicKey, deviceID, dev)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("boxID = %v, want nil", err)
	}
	// The Login request expects getDeviceId()'s "B" + smid string.
	if got != "Bsmid-test-0123456789" {
		t.Errorf("boxID = %q, want %q", got, "Bsmid-test-0123456789")
	}
	if ft.content != "application/octet-stream" {
		t.Errorf("Content-Type = %q, want application/octet-stream", ft.content)
	}

	// The POSTed body must carry the exact native `w1` field names:
	// organization, os, appId, encode (2), compress (3), data, tn, ep. The
	// real first request carries no `retry` field (only the background resend
	// adds it).
	var profile map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(ft.body, &profile); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("POSTed body is not JSON: %v", err)
	}
	for key, want := range map[string]any{
		"organization": Organization,
		"os":           OSName,
		"appId":        AppID,
		"encode":       2.0,
		"compress":     3.0,
	} {
		if got, ok := profile[key]; !ok || got != want {
			t.Errorf("profile[%q] = %v (present=%v), want %v", key, got, ok, want)
		}
	}
	if _, hasRetry := profile["retry"]; hasRetry {
		t.Errorf("profile carries an unexpected \"retry\" field (the first request has none)")
	}
	fields := map[string]string{}
	for _, key := range []string{"data", "tn", "ep"} {
		v, ok := profile[key].(string)
		if !ok || v == "" {
			t.Fatalf("profile[%q] = %v, want a non-empty protected value", key, profile[key])
		}
		fields[key] = v
	}
	if plaintext, want := unprotect(t, priv, fields["data"], fields["ep"], fields["tn"]), mustDeviceData(t, deviceID, dev); plaintext != want {
		t.Errorf("decrypted data = %q, want deviceData(%q) = %q", plaintext, deviceID, want)
	}
}

// testInstall is a filled install with pinned values, so deviceData's output is

// mustDeviceData is deviceData, failing the test on an error.
func mustDeviceData(t *testing.T, deviceID string, d Device) string {
	t.Helper()
	s, err := deviceData(deviceID, d)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deviceData = %v", err)
	}

// TestBoxIDErrors covers the replies BoxID must refuse: a non-200 status, the
// server's 1902 with no deviceId (ErrUnassigned), and a body that isn't JSON.
func TestBoxIDErrors(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name       string
		status     int
		body       string
		unassigned bool
	}{
		// A success-shaped body, so only the status check can reject it.
		{"non-200", http.StatusInternalServerError, `{"code":1100,"detail":{"deviceId":"smid-1"}}`, false},
		{"1902 without deviceId", http.StatusOK, `{"code":1902,"detail":{},"requestId":"r-1"}`, true},
		{"malformed JSON", http.StatusOK, "not json", false},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			client := &http.Client{Transport: roundTripperFunc(func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
				return &http.Response{
					StatusCode: c.status,
					Body:       io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(c.body)),
					Header:     http.Header{},
				}, nil
			})}

			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("BoxID = %q, nil; want an error", boxID)
			}
			if got := errors.Is(err, ErrUnassigned); got != c.unassigned {
				t.Errorf("errors.Is(%v, ErrUnassigned) = %v, want %v", err, got, c.unassigned)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestBoxIDNeedsInstall checks BoxID refuses an install with values unset
// before it contacts the server, rather than register a phone the caller
// never sees and so can't keep.
func TestBoxIDNeedsInstall(t *testing.T) {
	calls := 0
	client := &http.Client{Transport: roundTripperFunc(func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
		calls++
		return nil, errors.New("unexpected request")
	})}
	boxID, err := BoxID(client, "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_n3d", Device{})
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unset") || calls != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BoxID with no install = %q, %v after %d requests; want the unset-install error and no request", boxID, err, calls)
	}
}

// roundTripperFunc adapts a func to http.RoundTripper.
type roundTripperFunc func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error)

func (f roundTripperFunc) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	return f(req)
}

// TestProtectRoundTrip inverts the whole native `w1` pipeline. protect takes
// the RSA key as a parameter, so a test-generated key pair can decrypt ep back
// to r.
func TestProtectRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	priv, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rsa.GenerateKey = %v", err)
	}
	in := mustDeviceData(t, "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_n3d", Device{Install: testInstall}.withHostDefaults())
	data, ep, tn, err := protect(&priv.PublicKey, in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("protect = %v", err)
	}
	if got := unprotect(t, priv, data, ep, tn); got != in {
		t.Errorf("inflate(decrypt(data)) = %q, want the device-data JSON", got)
	}
}

// unprotect inverts protect with the test's private key and returns the
// inflated device data, failing the test at the first malformed stage. The AES
// key is derived here from the spec (hex MD5 of r), not via aesKeyFromNonce, so
// a broken helper can't cancel itself out.
func unprotect(t *testing.T, priv *rsa.PrivateKey, data, ep, tn string) string {
	t.Helper()
	oaepDecrypt := func(name, s string) []byte {
		ct, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(s)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s is not base64: %v", name, err)
		}
		pt, err := rsa.DecryptOAEP(sha256.New(), nil, priv, ct, nil)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: RSA-OAEP(SHA-256) decrypt = %v", name, err)
		}
		return pt
	}

	// ep wraps the 16-char alphanumeric nonce r; tn wraps "0".
	r := oaepDecrypt("ep", ep)
	if len(r) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("ep plaintext = %q, want the 16-char nonce", r)
	}
	const alnum = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
	for _, c := range string(r) {
		if !strings.ContainsRune(alnum, c) {
			t.Fatalf("ep plaintext = %q, want alphanumeric", r)
		}
	}
	if got := string(oaepDecrypt("tn", tn)); got != "0" {
		t.Errorf("tn plaintext = %q, want \"0\"", got)
	}

	// data = base64(AES-256-CBC(rawDeflate(in), hex(MD5(r)), IV "0102030405060708")).
	sum := md5.Sum(r)
	block, err := aes.NewCipher([]byte(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("aes.NewCipher = %v", err)
	}
	ct, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("data is not base64: %v", err)
	}
	if len(ct) == 0 || len(ct)%aes.BlockSize != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("data length = %d, want a non-zero multiple of %d", len(ct), aes.BlockSize)
	}
	pt := make([]byte, len(ct))
	cipher.NewCBCDecrypter(block, []byte("0102030405060708")).CryptBlocks(pt, ct)
	pad := int(pt[len(pt)-1])
	if pad < 1 || pad > aes.BlockSize || !bytes.Equal(pt[len(pt)-pad:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{byte(pad)}, pad)) {
		t.Fatalf("decrypted data ends in % x, want PKCS#7 padding", pt[len(pt)-aes.BlockSize:])
	}
	inflated, err := io.ReadAll(flate.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(pt[:len(pt)-pad])))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("raw inflate = %v", err)
	}
	return string(inflated)
}

// TestProtectWithEmbeddedKey checks the embedded iShumei key parses as 2048-bit
// RSA: its OAEP ciphertexts are 256 bytes, i.e. 344 base64 chars.
func TestProtectWithEmbeddedKey(t *testing.T) {

		}
	}
}

// TestAESKeyFromNonce pins the key derivation to a known answer: the
// lowercase-hex MD5 of r.
func TestAESKeyFromNonce(t *testing.T) {
	const want = "19fc8eff82037f1fc0d8ea1d32b5e339" // md5("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP")
	if got := string(aesKeyFromNonce("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP")); got != want {
		t.Errorf("aesKeyFromNonce = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

// decodeDeviceData parses deviceData's JSON, keeping numbers exact.
func decodeDeviceData(t *testing.T, s string) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(s))
	dec.UseNumber()
	var m map[string]any
	if err := dec.Decode(&m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deviceData is not valid JSON: %v\n%s", err, s)
	}
	return m
}

// TestDeviceData checks the fields deviceData adds to the template, and that it
// serializes the way the SDK does: compact, without empty top-level entries,
// and without Wi-Fi details by default. A broken template only shows up live as
// a 1902, so this is also the guard against hand edits.
func TestDeviceData(t *testing.T) {
	const id = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_n3d"
	// The SDK started one second before collecting, at 1790882443713, whose
	// java.util.Random digits TestJavaRandomDigits pins.
	d := testDevice()
	s := mustDeviceData(t, id, d)

	var compact bytes.Buffer
	if err := json.Compact(&compact, []byte(s)); err != nil || compact.String() != s {
		t.Errorf("deviceData is not compact JSON (Compact error %v):\n%s", err, s)
	}
	m := decodeDeviceData(t, s)
	for key, want := range map[string]string{
		"a2":   id,
		"a97":  id,
		"a9":   "1790882444713",
		"a40":  "1790000000000",
		"a171": "882444713",
		"a170": "882444713",
		"a80":  "1790882443713-36769",
		"a133": "287",
		"a24":  testInstall.AndroidID,
		"a84":  testInstall.MediaDrmID,
		"a163": testInstall.PUUID,
		"a125": "map[fit:1775000000000 lut:1789000000000]",
		// No smid cached yet: the cache file doesn't exist, so both are 0.
		"a167": "0",
		"a168": "0",
	} {
		if got := fmt.Sprint(m[key]); got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", key, got, want)
		}
	}
	for _, key := range []string{"a19", "a30", "a31"} {
		if v, ok := m[key]; ok {
			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want it absent: a real Last War install reads no Wi-Fi details", key, v)
		}
	}
	if v, ok := m["a126"]; ok {
		t.Errorf("a126 = %v, want it absent before the install's first registration", v)
	}
	for key, v := range m {
		if isEmpty(v) {
			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want empty entries dropped, as the SDK's serializer does", key, v)
		}
	}
	// false and 0 aren't empty to the SDK, so they stay.
	if m["a117"] != false || fmt.Sprint(m["a113"]) != "0" {
		t.Errorf("a117 = %v, a113 = %v, want false and 0 kept", m["a117"], m["a113"])
	}

	backwards := d
	backwards.Now, backwards.BootTime = d.BootTime, d.Now
	if _, err := deviceData(id, backwards); err == nil {
		t.Error("deviceData with the boot time after the collection time = nil error, want an error")
	}
	unset := d
	unset.Install = Install{}
	if _, err := deviceData(id, unset); err == nil {
		t.Error("deviceData with no install values = nil error, want an error")
	}
	for name, unsetOne := range map[string]func(*Install){
		"androidId":        func(in *Install) { in.AndroidID = "" },
		"mediaDrmId":       func(in *Install) { in.MediaDrmID = "" },
		"puuid":            func(in *Install) { in.PUUID = "" },
		"firstInstallTime": func(in *Install) { in.FirstInstallTime = time.Time{} },
		"lastUpdateTime":   func(in *Install) { in.LastUpdateTime = time.Time{} },
	} {
		partial := d
		unsetOne(&partial.Install)
		if _, err := deviceData(id, partial); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("deviceData with the install's %s unset = nil error, want an error", name)
		}
	}
	invalid := d
	invalid.Install.AndroidID = "not-an-android-id"
	if _, err := deviceData(id, invalid); err == nil {
		t.Error("deviceData with an invalid androidId = nil error, want an error")
	}
	other := d
	other.Install.DeviceID = "another-device"
	if _, err := deviceData(id, other); err == nil {
		t.Error("deviceData with another deviceId's install = nil error, want an error")
	}
}

// TestDeviceDataRegistered checks a registered install sends its cached box ID
// back as a126, with its save time in a167 and a168.
func TestDeviceDataRegistered(t *testing.T) {
	d := testDevice()
	d.Install, _ = d.Install.Registered("Bsmid-earlier", time.UnixMilli(1789500000123))
	m := decodeDeviceData(t, mustDeviceData(t, "id", d))
	for key, want := range map[string]string{
		"a126": "Bsmid-earlier",
		"a167": "1789500000123",
		"a168": "1789500000123",
	} {
		if got := fmt.Sprint(m[key]); got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s = %s, want %s", key, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestDeviceDataWiFi checks a Device's Wi-Fi details land the way WifiInfo
// reports them: the SSID in quotes, without HTML escaping.
func TestDeviceDataWiFi(t *testing.T) {
	d := testDevice()
	d.WiFi = &WiFi{SSID: "Home <5G> & co", BSSID: "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff", IP: "192.168.1.50"}
	s := mustDeviceData(t, "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_n3d", d)
	if strings.Contains(s, `\u00`) {
		t.Errorf("deviceData escapes characters the SDK sends raw:\n%s", s)
	}
	m := decodeDeviceData(t, s)
	for key, want := range map[string]string{
		"a19": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff",
		"a30": `"Home <5G> & co"`,
		"a31": "192.168.1.50",
	} {
		if m[key] != want {
			t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %q", key, m[key], want)
		}
	}

	// An unreadable host IP leaves a31 empty, so it's dropped.
	d.WiFi = &WiFi{SSID: "Home"}
	if m := decodeDeviceData(t, mustDeviceData(t, "id", d)); m["a31"] != nil || m["a19"] != nil {
		t.Errorf("a31 = %v, a19 = %v, want both dropped when empty", m["a31"], m["a19"])
	}
}

// TestWithHostDefaults checks zero fields take the host's values and set ones
// stay, without changing the caller's WiFi.
func TestWithHostDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	before := time.Now()
	d := Device{}.withHostDefaults()
	if d.Now.Before(before) || d.Now.After(time.Now()) {
		t.Errorf("Now = %v, want the current time", d.Now)
	}
	if d.BootTime.After(d.Now) {
		t.Errorf("BootTime = %v, want it no later than Now %v", d.BootTime, d.Now)
	}
	// A set Now keeps the host's uptime: the boot time moves with it.
	moved := Device{Now: time.UnixMilli(1790882444713)}.withHostDefaults()
	if diff := moved.Now.Sub(moved.BootTime) - hostUptime(); diff < -time.Second || diff > time.Second {
		t.Errorf("BootTime = %v for Now %v, want Now minus the host's uptime %v", moved.BootTime, moved.Now, hostUptime())
	}
	if d.WiFi != nil {
		t.Errorf("WiFi = %+v, want nil: no Wi-Fi details unless asked for", d.WiFi)
	}
	if d.CollectTime < 150*time.Millisecond || d.CollectTime >= 600*time.Millisecond {
		t.Errorf("CollectTime = %v, want 150 to 600 ms", d.CollectTime)
	}
	if d.Install != (Install{}) {
		t.Errorf("Install = %+v, want it left empty: withHostDefaults never makes up install values", d.Install)
	}
	if kept := testDevice().withHostDefaults(); kept.Install != testInstall || kept.CollectTime != 287*time.Millisecond {
		t.Errorf("withHostDefaults changed a set Install or CollectTime: %+v, %v", kept.Install, kept.CollectTime)
	}

	set := Device{Now: time.UnixMilli(2), BootTime: time.UnixMilli(1), WiFi: &WiFi{SSID: "Home"}}
	got := set.withHostDefaults()
	if !got.Now.Equal(set.Now) || !got.BootTime.Equal(set.BootTime) {
		t.Errorf("withHostDefaults changed set clocks: %v, %v", got.Now, got.BootTime)
	}
	if got.WiFi.IP != hostIP() || got.WiFi.SSID != "Home" {
		t.Errorf("WiFi = %+v, want SSID kept and IP %q from the host", got.WiFi, hostIP())
	}
	if set.WiFi.IP != "" {
		t.Errorf("withHostDefaults wrote the IP into the caller's WiFi")
	}
}

// TestUptime checks the host's uptime reads on the systems that support it.
func TestUptime(t *testing.T) {
	if runtime.GOOS != "linux" && runtime.GOOS != "darwin" {
		t.Skip("uptime reads only Linux and macOS")
	}
	got, err := uptime()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("uptime = %v", err)
	}
	if got <= 0 || got > 10*365*24*time.Hour {
		t.Errorf("uptime = %v, want a positive duration under ten years", got)
	}
}

// TestJavaRandomDigits pins the java.util.Random port to known answers from
// OpenJDK 27: five `new Random(seed).nextInt(10)` draws per seed.
func TestJavaRandomDigits(t *testing.T) {
	for seed, want := range map[int64]string{
		0:             "08975",
		1:             "58734",
		1784568338000: "17865",
		1790882443713: "36769",
		1791999999999: "48223",
	} {
		if got := javaRandomDigits(seed, 5); got != want {
			t.Errorf("javaRandomDigits(%d, 5) = %q, want %q", seed, got, want)
		}
	}
}
```

`internal/shumei/uptime_darwin.go`:

```go
//go:build darwin

package shumei

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)

// uptime is the time since kern.boottime, a struct timeval: int64 seconds,
// then int32 microseconds, little-endian on both macOS architectures.
// syscall.Sysctl drops one trailing NUL byte, which can only come from the
// timeval's padding.
func uptime() (time.Duration, error) {
	s, err := syscall.Sysctl("kern.boottime")
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	b := []byte(s)
	if len(b) < 12 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("shumei: kern.boottime is %d bytes, want a timeval", len(b))
	}
	sec := int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[:8]))
	usec := int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[8:12]))
	return time.Since(time.Unix(sec, usec*int64(time.Microsecond))), nil
}
```

`internal/shumei/uptime_linux.go`:

```go
//go:build linux

package shumei

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// uptime reads /proc/uptime's first field: seconds since boot, suspend
// included (CLOCK_BOOTTIME, the clock Android's elapsedRealtime() reads).
func uptime() (time.Duration, error) {
	b, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/uptime")
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	field, _, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)), " ")
	secs, err := strconv.ParseFloat(field, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("shumei: parse /proc/uptime %q: %w", field, err)
	}
	return time.Duration(secs * float64(time.Second)), nil
}
```

`internal/testutil/gsl_decrypt.go`:

```go
package testutil

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"lastwar-client/internal/crypto"
	"lastwar-client/internal/gsl"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
)

// UseDecryptingGSL is UseInMemoryGSL with a fake that also reads the requests: it keeps the RSA
// private key behind the check-version reply's public key, decrypts each getserverlist.php form
// the way the server does, and records it. gslResponses answer the calls in order, repeating the
// last. forms returns the decoded forms so far.
func UseDecryptingGSL(t *testing.T, gslResponses ...gsl.LoginServerListRespon) (client *http.Client, forms func() []url.Values) {
	t.Helper()
	priv, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("generate RSA key: %v", err)
	}
	der, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(&priv.PublicKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("marshal public key: %v", err)
	}
	pub := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(der)

	var mu sync.Mutex
	var got []url.Values
	call := 0
	handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch {
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "getlsu3dversion.php"):
			_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(gsl.CheckVersionResponse{ResMsg: gsl.FlexString(pub)})
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "getserverlist.php"):
			form := url.Values{}
			if err := r.ParseForm(); err == nil {
				saltCT, _ := crypto.URLSafeB64Decode(r.FormValue("uuid"))
				if salt, err := rsa.DecryptPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, priv, saltCT); err == nil { //nolint:staticcheck // SA1019: the fake server mirrors the protocol's PKCS#1 v1.5 salt
					data, _ := crypto.URLSafeB64Decode(r.FormValue("data"))
					if plain, err := crypto.AESECBDecryptPKCS7(data, crypto.MD5HexKey(string(salt))); err == nil {
						form, _ = url.ParseQuery(string(plain))
					}
				}
			}
			mu.Lock()
			got = append(got, form)
			idx := min(call, len(gslResponses)-1)
			call++
			mu.Unlock()
			_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(gslResponses[idx])
		default:
			http.NotFound(w, r)
		}
	})

	orig := gsl.CheckVersionHosts
	gsl.CheckVersionHosts = []string{"http://gsl.invalid"}
	t.Cleanup(func() { gsl.CheckVersionHosts = orig })
	return &http.Client{Transport: recorderRoundTripper{h: handler}}, func() []url.Values {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		return append([]url.Values(nil), got...)
	}
}
```

`internal/testutil/testutil.go`:

```go
// Package testutil holds test helpers shared across the internal packages
// (packet encoders, an RSA pubkey generator, a fake net.Error, and small conversions).
package testutil

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"lastwar-client/internal/gsl"
	"lastwar-client/internal/sfs"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
)

// CaptureStdout redirects os.Stdout to a pipe for the duration of fn and
// returns everything written to it. DecodeStreamFile writes directly via
// fmt.Printf rather than accepting an io.Writer, so this is the only way to
// observe its per-packet output (as opposed to just its returned error).
//
// The drain runs in a goroutine concurrently with fn, not after it: an
// os.Pipe has a small fixed kernel buffer, and DecodeStreamFile can print
// more than that fits, so a synchronous "run fn, then read" would deadlock
// with fn blocked on a full pipe and nothing reading it yet.
func CaptureStdout(t *testing.T, fn func()) string {
	t.Helper()
	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("os.Pipe: %v", err)
	}
	orig := os.Stdout
	os.Stdout = w
	t.Cleanup(func() { os.Stdout = orig })

	outCh := make(chan string, 1)
	go func() {
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		_, _ = io.Copy(&buf, r)
		outCh <- buf.String()
	}()

	fn()

	os.Stdout = orig
	if err := w.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("close pipe writer: %v", err)
	}
	out := <-outCh
	_ = r.Close()
	return out
}

// MustEncodeCorruptPacket builds a packet whose framing is entirely valid
// (correct length prefix, correctly round-trips through sfs.ReadPacket) but
// whose sfs.SFSObject body is not: the leading tag byte is overwritten so
// DecodeObject's "expected top-level tag 18" check fails. This is the
// packet-framing-succeeded-but-content-is-garbage case, as distinct from a
// truncated/corrupt frame (which sfs.ReadPacket itself rejects).
func MustEncodeCorruptPacket(t *testing.T, field, value string) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	o := sfs.NewSFSObject()
	o.PutUtfString(field, value)
	body, err := sfs.EncodeObject(o)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("sfs.EncodeObject: %v", err)
	}
	body[0] = 0xEE // not sfs.SFSObjectType (18) -> DecodeObject must error
	packet, err := sfs.EncodePacket(body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("sfs.EncodePacket: %v", err)
	}
	return packet
}

// RSAPubKeyDER returns a fresh 2048-bit RSA public key, DER+base64 encoded, for the game
// package's fake-GSL-server tests. Duplicated from internal/gsl's own copy: test helpers can't be
// shared across package boundaries.
func RSAPubKeyDER(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	priv, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("generate RSA key: %v", err)
	}
	der, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(&priv.PublicKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("marshal public key: %v", err)
	}
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(der)
}

// FlexPort converts a plain int port into gsl.go's gsl.FlexString shape, for building test
// gsl.LoginServerInfo/gsl.AccountServerInfo fixtures now that Port/WsPort are gsl.FlexString (round 35 --
// see gsl.FlexString.Int's own doc comment in gsl.go for why).
func FlexPort(n int) gsl.FlexString { return gsl.FlexString(strconv.Itoa(n)) }

// FakeTimeoutNetError is a minimal net.Error whose Timeout() reports true, standing in for the
// *net.OpError a real deadline-exceeded net.Conn.Write returns -- per net.Conn's documented
// contract, "a Write ... that exceeds the [write] deadline ... returns an error that wraps
// os.ErrDeadlineExceeded" and satisfies net.Error with Timeout() == true. Used by
// TestSendAndWaitWriteStageFailureIsNonTimeoutNetError below to prove sendAndWait's write-stage
// wrapper (sendStageError, conn.go) forces Timeout()==false even when the underlying cause is
// itself exactly this Timeout()==true shape.
type FakeTimeoutNetError struct{ Msg string }

func (e FakeTimeoutNetError) Error() string { return e.Msg }
func (FakeTimeoutNetError) Timeout() bool   { return true }
func (FakeTimeoutNetError) Temporary() bool { return true }

// SplitHostPortInt parses a "host:port" address (as returned by net.Listener.Addr().String())
// into DoCrossServerLogin's IP/Port shape.
func SplitHostPortInt(t *testing.T, addr string) (string, int) {
	t.Helper()
	host, portStr, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("split host/port %q: %v", addr, err)
	}
	port, err := strconv.Atoi(portStr)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse port %q: %v", portStr, err)
	}
	return host, port
}

// NewFakeGSLServer stands up one httptest.Server answering both gsl.CheckVersion's
// getlsu3dversion.php (always the same canned response, carrying a throwaway RSA pubkey) and
// gsl.GetServerList's getserverlist.php (like TestGetServerListAgainstFakeServer, a plaintext --
// unencrypted -- gsl.LoginServerListRespon body, which gsl.GetServerList already falls back to when no
// "bin" field is present). gslResponses is consumed one entry per gsl.GetServerList POST, in order;
// once exhausted, the last entry repeats, so a test only needs to supply as many entries as it
// cares to distinguish (one per distinct gsl.GetServerList call it expects, e.g. the initial
// opt=new/fix/login call and, separately, any mid-redirect opt=fix refresh call).
func NewFakeGSLServer(t *testing.T, gslResponses ...gsl.LoginServerListRespon) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	server := httptest.NewServer(gslHandler(t, gslResponses))
	t.Cleanup(server.Close)
	return server
}

// gslHandler is the shared request handler behind both NewFakeGSLServer (over a real httptest.Server)
// and UseInMemoryGSL (over an in-memory RoundTripper): it answers gsl.CheckVersion's
// getlsu3dversion.php with a canned throwaway RSA pubkey and gsl.GetServerList's getserverlist.php
// with the next gslResponses entry (repeating the last once exhausted -- see NewFakeGSLServer's doc
// comment for the per-call semantics).
func gslHandler(t *testing.T, gslResponses []gsl.LoginServerListRespon) http.HandlerFunc {
	t.Helper()
	pub := RSAPubKeyDER(t)
	var mu sync.Mutex
	call := 0
	return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		switch {
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "getlsu3dversion.php"):
			_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(gsl.CheckVersionResponse{ResMsg: gsl.FlexString(pub)})
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "getserverlist.php"):
			mu.Lock()
			idx := call
			if idx >= len(gslResponses) {
				idx = len(gslResponses) - 1
			}
			call++
			mu.Unlock()
			_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(gslResponses[idx])
		default:
			http.NotFound(w, r)
		}
	}
}

// UseFakeGSLServer points gsl.CheckVersionHosts at server for the duration of the test, restoring the
// real list on cleanup -- same override pattern as gsl_http_test.go's gsl.CheckVersion tests.
func UseFakeGSLServer(t *testing.T, server *httptest.Server) {
	t.Helper()
	orig := gsl.CheckVersionHosts
	gsl.CheckVersionHosts = []string{server.URL}
	t.Cleanup(func() { gsl.CheckVersionHosts = orig })
}

// recorderRoundTripper serves each request synchronously by replaying it through an http.Handler and
// recording the response, with NO real socket and NO background goroutines -- unlike httptest.Server,
// which is a real loopback listener whose http.Transport client pool leaves keep-alive reader
// goroutines parked in the netpoller. That difference is what makes this usable inside a
// testing/synctest bubble: a plain RoundTripper call is an ordinary function call the bubble can run
// deterministically, whereas real HTTP would block in the netpoller (never durably, so time can't
// advance) and strand Transport goroutines that trip synctest's end-of-bubble "still running" check.
type recorderRoundTripper struct{ h http.Handler }

func (rt recorderRoundTripper) RoundTrip(r *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	rt.h.ServeHTTP(rec, r)
	return rec.Result(), nil
}

// UseInMemoryGSL is the synctest-friendly sibling of NewFakeGSLServer+UseFakeGSLServer: it points
// gsl.CheckVersionHosts at a dummy URL (the RoundTripper ignores the host, dispatching purely on the
// request path) and returns an *http.Client whose transport answers CheckVersion/GetServerList
// entirely in memory -- same canned responses, no real network, no goroutines, no client Timeout
// (so no timer goroutine either). Pass the returned client as crossServerTestOpts.httpClient so a
// runCrossServerTest test's GSL round-trips run inside a synctest bubble under virtual time.
func UseInMemoryGSL(t *testing.T, gslResponses ...gsl.LoginServerListRespon) *http.Client {
	t.Helper()
	orig := gsl.CheckVersionHosts
	gsl.CheckVersionHosts = []string{"http://gsl.invalid"}
	t.Cleanup(func() { gsl.CheckVersionHosts = orig })
	return &http.Client{Transport: recorderRoundTripper{h: gslHandler(t, gslResponses)}}
}
```
